118	class FusedLinearGRPOFunction(FusedLinearPPOBase):
119	    @staticmethod
120	    def ppo_loss_fn(
121	        per_token_logps,
122	        attention_mask,
123	        advantages,
124	        full_attention_mask,
125	        ref_per_token_logps=None,  # shape: [chunk_size, seq_len]
126	        old_per_token_logps=None,
127	        epsilon_low=0.2,
128	        epsilon_high=0.2,
129	        beta=0.04,
130	        loss_type="dapo",  # ["grpo", "bnpo", "dr_grpo", "dapo", "cispo", "sapo", "luspo", "vespo"]
131	        max_completion_length=None,  # Required for dr_grpo
132	        importance_sampling_level="token",  # ["token", "sequence"] - new parameter for GSPO
133	        sapo_temperature_pos=1.0,  # Temperature for positive advantages in SAPO
134	        sapo_temperature_neg=1.05,  # Temperature for negative advantages in SAPO
135	        vllm_is_ratio=None,  # vLLM importance sampling ratio (chunk_size, seq_len) or (chunk_size, 1) or None
136	        delta=None,  # Upper clamp for two-sided clipping (INTELLECT-2)
137	        use_bias_correction_kl=False,  # Importance-sampling-corrected KL (DeepSeek-V3.2)
138	        vespo_k_pos=2.0,  # VESPO gamma shape k for non-negative advantages
139	        vespo_lambda_pos=3.0,  # VESPO gamma rate lambda for non-negative advantages
140	        vespo_k_neg=3.0,  # VESPO gamma shape k for negative advantages
141	        vespo_lambda_neg=2.0,  # VESPO gamma rate lambda for negative advantages
142	        num_items_in_batch=None,  # Total active tokens across the entire generation batch (TRL-compat)
143	        **kwargs,
144	    ):
145	        """GRPO Loss Function matching GRPOTrainer implementation."""
146	        # Validate sequence-level + loss_type combinations
147	        if importance_sampling_level == "sequence" and loss_type in ("cispo", "sapo", "vespo"):
148	            raise ValueError(
149	                f"Sequence-level importance sampling is not supported for loss_type='{loss_type}'. "
150	                f"Use importance_sampling_level='token' instead."
151	            )
152	
153	        # Get reference model probabilities
154	        if ref_per_token_logps is None:
155	            ref_per_token_logps = per_token_logps.detach()
156	
157	        # Compute policy gradient loss with importance sampling ratio
158	        old_per_token_logps = old_per_token_logps if old_per_token_logps is not None else per_token_logps.detach()
159	        log_ratio = per_token_logps - old_per_token_logps
160	
161	        if importance_sampling_level == "token":
162	            log_importance_weights = log_ratio
163	        elif importance_sampling_level == "sequence":
164	            log_importance_weights = (log_ratio * attention_mask).sum(-1) / attention_mask.sum(-1).clamp(min=1.0)
165	            log_importance_weights = log_importance_weights.unsqueeze(-1)
166	        else:
167	            raise ValueError(
168	                f"Unknown importance sampling level: {importance_sampling_level}. Possible values are 'token' "
169	                "and 'sequence'."
170	            )
171	
172	        # From here, log_importance_weights (and all subsequent tensors, coef_1, coef_2, etc.) shape depends on
173	        # importance_sampling_level: "token" level: (B, T); "sequence" level: (B, 1)
174	        coef_1 = torch.exp(log_importance_weights)
175	        coef_2, is_lower_clipped, is_upper_clipped = clip_coef_fn(coef_1, epsilon_low, epsilon_high, loss_type)
176	        if loss_type == "cispo":
177	            # CISPO: clip and detach the importance weights, multiply by log probs
178	            # Reference: https://github.com/huggingface/trl/blob/035c3ff151b953ca72cdfe0ee966bc1469a26fde/trl/trainer/grpo_trainer.py#L2030
179	            per_token_loss = -coef_2 * advantages.unsqueeze(1) * per_token_logps
180	        elif loss_type == "sapo":
181	            # SAPO: Soft Adaptive Policy Optimization
182	            # Uses sigmoid-based soft gating instead of hard clipping
183	            # Reference: https://huggingface.co/papers/2511.20347
184	            # TRL implementation: https://github.com/huggingface/trl/blob/1bd2a52ec2d8344050af736d60cdc735181ae4b8/trl/trainer/grpo_trainer.py#L2037-L2046
185	            advantages_expanded = advantages.unsqueeze(1).expand_as(coef_1)
186	            positive_advantages_mask = advantages_expanded > 0
187	
188	            # torch.where over both branches rather than boolean-mask assignment:
189	            # mask indexing lowers to aten.nonzero, which graph-breaks under
190	            # torch.compile. sapo_loss_fn is elementwise so this is identical.
191	            per_token_loss = torch.where(
192	                positive_advantages_mask,
193	                sapo_loss_fn(coef_1, sapo_temperature_pos),
194	                sapo_loss_fn(coef_1, sapo_temperature_neg),
195	            )
196	            per_token_loss = -per_token_loss * advantages_expanded
197	        elif loss_type == "vespo":
198	            # VESPO: Value-Enhanced Sequence-level Policy Optimization.
199	            # Uses a detached gamma weighting phi(w) as a gradient scaling coefficient.
200	            # Reference: TRL grpo_trainer.get_gamma_weights. The vllm correction for
201	            # distribution mismatch is folded into phi_seq via ``importance_sampling_ratio``
202	            # rather than multiplying per_token_loss.
203	            phi_seq = get_gamma_weights(
204	                advantages=advantages,
205	                log_ratio_per_token=log_ratio,
206	                mask=attention_mask,
207	                importance_sampling_ratio=vllm_is_ratio,
208	                k_pos=vespo_k_pos,
209	                lambda_pos=vespo_lambda_pos,
210	                k_neg=vespo_k_neg,
211	                lambda_neg=vespo_lambda_neg,
212	            )
213	            per_token_loss = -phi_seq * advantages.unsqueeze(1) * per_token_logps
214	        else:
215	            # Apply delta (two-sided clipping from INTELLECT-2) to coef_1
216	            if delta is not None:
217	                coef_1 = torch.clamp(coef_1, max=delta)
218	            per_token_loss1 = coef_1 * advantages.unsqueeze(1)
219	            per_token_loss2 = coef_2 * advantages.unsqueeze(1)
220	            per_token_loss = -torch.min(per_token_loss1, per_token_loss2)
221	
222	        # Apply vLLM importance sampling correction BEFORE adding KL penalty
223	        # VESPO folds this correction into phi_seq (in log space), so we skip it here.
224	        if vllm_is_ratio is not None and loss_type != "vespo":
225	            per_token_loss = per_token_loss * vllm_is_ratio
226	
227	        if beta != 0.0:
228	            # Compute KL penalty (approximates KL[per_token_logps, ref_per_token_logps])
229	            kl_div = k3_loss_fn(ref_per_token_logps, per_token_logps)
230	            if use_bias_correction_kl:
231	                # Importance-sampling-corrected KL (DeepSeek-V3.2): kl *= coef_1.
232	                # Use exp(log_importance_weights) so the ratio's shape matches
233	                # importance_sampling_level (token: (B, T); sequence: (B, 1)),
234	                # mirroring TRL's ``per_token_kl * coef_1`` (un-clamped, before delta).
235	                kl_div = kl_div * torch.exp(log_importance_weights)
236	            # Combine losses
237	            per_token_loss = per_token_loss + beta * kl_div
238	
239	        # Note: We normalize by the number of tokens in the batch (using full_attention_mask),
240	        # which is consistent with the DAPO loss implementation (https://arxiv.org/html/2503.14476v1)
241	        # and TRL GRPO implementation
242	        # (https://github.com/huggingface/trl/blob/e751a16df56e70190fb94bed4a2035eec3303777/trl/trainer/grpo_trainer.py#L966)
243	        if loss_type == "grpo" or loss_type == "sapo":
244	            # Average per-sequence loss (SAPO uses same normalization as GRPO)
245	            loss = (
246	                (per_token_loss * attention_mask).sum(-1) / torch.clamp(attention_mask.sum(-1), min=1.0)
247	            ).sum() / full_attention_mask.shape[0]
248	        elif loss_type == "bnpo":
249	            # Batch Normalized Per-token loss (original implementation)
250	            loss = (per_token_loss * attention_mask).sum() / torch.clamp(full_attention_mask.sum(), min=1.0)
251	        elif loss_type == "dr_grpo":
252	            # Dimension-Reduced GRPO (normalize by batch_size * max_completion_length)
253	            if max_completion_length is None:
254	                raise ValueError("max_completion_length must be provided for loss_type 'dr_grpo'")
255	            loss = (per_token_loss * attention_mask).sum() / (full_attention_mask.shape[0] * max_completion_length)
256	        elif loss_type in ("dapo", "cispo", "vespo"):
257	            loss_normalizer = FusedLinearPPOBase._compute_dapo_normalizer(
258	                full_attention_mask, num_items_in_batch=num_items_in_batch
259	            )
260	            loss = (per_token_loss * attention_mask).sum() / loss_normalizer
261	        elif loss_type == "luspo":
262	            # Match TRL exactly: loss = (per_token_loss * mask.sum(1, keepdim=True)).mean()
263	            weighted = per_token_loss * attention_mask.sum(1, keepdim=True)
264	            loss = weighted.sum() / (full_attention_mask.shape[0] * weighted.shape[1])
265	        else:
266	            raise ValueError(f"Unknown loss type: {loss_type}")
267	
268	        # Calculate metrics
269	        metrics = []
270	        if beta != 0.0:
271	            metrics.append((kl_div * attention_mask).sum() / torch.clamp(full_attention_mask.sum(), min=1.0))
272	
273	        # Adjust clipping metric calculation based on importance sampling level
274	        if importance_sampling_level == "token":
275	            is_clipped = (is_lower_clipped & (advantages.unsqueeze(1) < 0)) | (
276	                is_upper_clipped & (advantages.unsqueeze(1) > 0)
277	            )
278	        else:  # sequence level
279	            # For sequence level, coef_1 is shape (B, 1), advantages is shape (B,)
280	            is_clipped = (is_lower_clipped & (advantages.unsqueeze(1) < 0)) | (
281	                is_upper_clipped & (advantages.unsqueeze(1) > 0)
282	            )
283	            is_clipped = is_clipped.expand_as(attention_mask)
284	
285	        metrics.append((is_clipped * attention_mask).sum() / torch.clamp(full_attention_mask.sum(), min=1.0))
286	        return loss, metrics

22	    def __init__(self, directory):

25	    def on_log(self, args, state, control, logs=None, **kwargs):
26	        with self.path.open("a") as stream:

30	class RecordedGRPO(GRPOTrainer):
31	    def __init__(self, *args, record_directory, record_tokens, **kwargs):
32	        self.record_directory = record_directory
33	        self.record_tokens = record_tokens
34	        self.record_index = 0
35	        self.capture_logps = False
36	        super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)

38	    def _get_per_token_logps_and_entropies(self, *args, **kwargs):
39	        result = super()._get_per_token_logps_and_entropies(*args, **kwargs)
40	        if self.capture_logps:
41	            self.recorded_logps = result[0].detach()
42	        return result
43	
44	    def _compute_loss(self, model, inputs):
45	        self.capture_logps = self.record_tokens and model.training
46	        loss = super()._compute_loss(model, inputs)
47	        if self.capture_logps:
48	            directory = self.record_directory / "token_records"

51	            previous = inputs.get("old_per_token_logps")
52	            previous = logps if previous is None else previous
53	            filename = f"step{self.state.global_step:04d}_batch{self.record_index:05d}_rank{self.accelerator.process_index}.npz"
54	            np.savez_compressed(

59	                mask=inputs["completion_mask"].detach().cpu().numpy(),

63	                generation_steps=self.args.steps_per_generation,

65	                clip_low=self.epsilon_low,

196	            we down-weight samples with low importance weights (when the importance sampling ratio < 1).
197	        vespo_lambda_pos (`float`, *optional*, defaults to `3.0`):

199	            aggressively we down-weight samples with high importance weights (when the importance sampling ratio > 1).
200	        vespo_k_neg (`float`, *optional*, defaults to `3.0`):
201	            k parameter for negative advantages, it is the power exponent in the VESPO loss. Controls how aggressively
202	            we down-weight samples with low importance weights (when the importance sampling ratio < 1).
203	        vespo_lambda_neg (`float`, *optional*, defaults to `2.0`):
204	            lambda parameter for negative advantages, it is the exponential decay factor in the VESPO loss. Controls
205	            how aggressively we down-weight samples with high importance weights (when the importance sampling ratio >
206	            1).
207	        importance_sampling_level (`str`, *optional*, defaults to `"token"`):
208	            Controls whether importance sampling ratios are computed at the `"token"` or `"sequence"` level. `"token"`
209	            keeps the raw per-token log-probability ratios (one weight per token). `"sequence"` averages the
210	            log-probability ratios across valid tokens to produce a single ratio per sequence. The [GSPO
211	            paper](https://huggingface.co/papers/2507.18071) shows that sequence-level sampling often yields more
212	            stable training and better alignment with sequence-level rewards.
213	        reward_weights (`list[float]`, *optional*):
214	            Weights for each reward function. Must match the number of reward functions. If `None`, all rewards are
215	            weighted equally with weight `1.0`.
216	        multi_objective_aggregation (`str`, *optional*, defaults to `"sum_then_normalize"`):
217	            Method to aggregate multiple reward functions. Supported values are:
218	
219	            - `"sum_then_normalize"` (default): First sums the weighted rewards from each reward function, then applies
220	              reward scaling/normalization as specified by `scale_rewards` (see `scale_rewards` for details).
221	            - `"normalize_then_sum"`: First normalizes/scales each reward function across generations (within each
222	              group), then sums the normalized rewards using the specified weights. The aggregated reward is then
223	              normalized at the batch level when forming advantages. This is the suggested approach from the paper
224	              [GDPO: Group reward-Decoupled Normalization Policy Optimization for Multi-reward RL
225	              Optimization](https://huggingface.co/papers/2601.05242).
226	        scale_rewards (`str` or `bool`, *optional*, defaults to `"group"`):
227	            Specifies the scaling strategy for rewards. Supported values are:
228	
229	            - `True` or `"group"` (default): rewards are scaled by the standard deviation within each group, ensuring
230	              unit variance within a group.
231	            - `"batch"`: rewards are scaled by the standard deviation across the entire batch, as recommended in the

234	              paper](https://huggingface.co/papers/2503.20783) recommends not scaling rewards, as scaling by the

236	        loss_type (`str`, *optional*, defaults to `"dapo"`):
237	            Specifies the loss formulation to use. Supported values are:
238	
239	            - `"grpo"`: Aggregates token-level losses by normalizing over sequence length. Not recommended due to
240	              length bias—this approach tends to prefer shorter completions with positive advantages and longer ones
241	              with negative advantages.
242	            - `"dr_grpo"`: Aggregates token-level losses by normalizing with a global constant. This method was
243	              introduced in the [Dr. GRPO paper](https://huggingface.co/papers/2503.20783) to eliminate length bias.
244	              The value of the constant corresponds to `max_completion_length`.
245	            - `"dapo"` (default): Aggregates token-level losses by normalizing with the number of active token in the
246	              global accumulated batch. This method was introduced in the [DAPO
247	              paper](https://huggingface.co/papers/2503.14476) to eliminate length bias.
248	            - `"bnpo"`: Aggregates token-level losses by normalizing with the number of active token in the local
249	              batch. Note that normalization is performed over the local batch only, so results may slightly vary
250	              depending on the local batch size, despite a constant effective batch size. When using

252	            - `"cispo"`: Clips the importance sampling weights instead of the advantage scaled importance weights. The

254	              losses are aggregated by normalizing with the number of active tokens in the global accumulated batch.

256	            - `"sapo"`: Soft Adaptive Policy Optimization loss, as introduced in the [Soft Adaptive Policy Optimization
257	              paper](https://huggingface.co/papers/2511.20347). Replaces hard clipping with a smooth,
258	              temperature-controlled gate that adaptively attenuates off-policy updates while preserving useful
259	              learning signals.
260	            - `"luspo"`: Length-Unbiased Sequence Policy Optimization loss. A sequence-level loss that scales each
261	              sequence's loss by its length. This is a modification of GSPO and requires
262	              `importance_sampling_level="sequence"`. Introduced in the [LUSPO
263	              paper](https://huggingface.co/papers/2602.05261).
264	            - `"vespo"`: Variational Sequence-Level Soft Policy Optimization. Replaces hard clipping with a smooth,
265	              asymmetric Gamma weighting function applied directly to sequence-level importance weights. Introduced in
266	              the [VESPO paper](https://huggingface.co/papers/2602.10693).
267	        mask_truncated_completions (`bool`, *optional*, defaults to `False`):
268	            When enabled, truncated completions are excluded from the loss calculation, preventing them from being
269	            incorrectly penalized and introducing noise during training. According to the
270	            [DAPO](https://huggingface.co/papers/2503.14476) paper, this is a good practice for training stability.
271	        sync_ref_model (`bool`, *optional*, defaults to `False`):
272	            Whether to synchronize the reference model with the active model every `ref_model_sync_steps` steps, using
273	            the `ref_model_mixup_alpha` parameter. This synchronization originates from the
274	            [TR-DPO](https://huggingface.co/papers/2404.09656) paper.
275	        ref_model_mixup_alpha (`float`, *optional*, defaults to `0.6`):
276	            α parameter from the [TR-DPO](https://huggingface.co/papers/2404.09656) paper, which controls the mix
277	            between the current policy and the previous reference policy during updates. The reference policy is
278	            updated according to the equation: `π_ref = α * π_θ + (1 - α) * π_ref_prev`. To use this parameter, you

281	            τ parameter from the [TR-DPO](https://huggingface.co/papers/2404.09656) paper, which determines how
282	            frequently the current policy is synchronized with the reference policy. To use this parameter, you must
283	            set `sync_ref_model=True`.

285	            ρ parameter from [Beyond the 80/20 Rule](https://huggingface.co/papers/2506.01939). Keeps in the policy

297	        use_adaptive_entropy (`bool`, *optional*, defaults to `False`):

333	                - `"sequence_truncate"`: Sequence-level truncated IS. A single sequence ratio is clipped to

30	def k3_loss_fn(log_p, log_q):
31	    # computes k3 estimate of KL[q, p]
32	    # ref: http://joschu.net/blog/kl-approx.html
33	    return torch.exp(log_p - log_q) - (log_p - log_q) - 1.0
34	
35	
36	@torch.no_grad()
37	def get_gamma_weights(
38	    advantages: torch.Tensor,
39	    log_ratio_per_token: torch.Tensor,
40	    mask: torch.Tensor,
41	    importance_sampling_ratio: torch.Tensor | None = None,
42	    k_pos: float = 2.0,
43	    lambda_pos: float = 3.0,
44	    k_neg: float = 3.0,
45	    lambda_neg: float = 2.0,
46	) -> torch.Tensor:
47	    """VESPO gamma weighting: phi(w) = e^lambda * w^k * e^{-lambda*w} (normalized so phi(1)=1).
48	
49	    Computed in log space and detached (via ``@torch.no_grad``) so ``phi_seq`` acts purely as a gradient-scaling
50	    coefficient. Returns a (B, 1) tensor. TRL reference: ``trl.trainer.grpo_trainer.GRPOTrainer.get_gamma_weights``.
51	    """
52	    lower_clamp = math.log(1e-8)
53	
54	    log_ratio_clamped = torch.clamp(log_ratio_per_token, -20.0, 20.0)
55	    seq_log_ratio = torch.sum(log_ratio_clamped * mask, dim=-1, keepdim=True)  # (B, 1)
56	
57	    if importance_sampling_ratio is not None:
58	        log_is_ratio = torch.clamp(torch.log(importance_sampling_ratio), lower_clamp, 20.0)
59	        seq_log_ratio = seq_log_ratio + torch.sum(log_is_ratio, dim=-1, keepdim=True)
60	
61	    log_w_seq = torch.clamp(seq_log_ratio, lower_clamp, 20.0)
62	    w_seq = torch.exp(log_w_seq)
63	
64	    is_nonneg_adv = advantages.unsqueeze(-1) >= 0
65	    k_seq = torch.where(is_nonneg_adv, k_pos, k_neg)
66	    lambda_seq = torch.where(is_nonneg_adv, lambda_pos, lambda_neg).clamp(min=1e-4)
67	
68	    log_phi = lambda_seq + k_seq * log_w_seq - lambda_seq * w_seq
69	    phi_seq = torch.exp(log_phi).nan_to_num(nan=0.0, posinf=0.0, neginf=0.0)
70	    return phi_seq
71	
72	
73	def sapo_loss_fn(importance_ratio: torch.Tensor, temperature: float) -> torch.Tensor:
74	    """SAPO (Soft Adaptive Policy Optimization) loss function.
75	
76	    Replaces hard clipping with a smooth, temperature-controlled gate that adaptively attenuates off-policy updates
77	    while preserving useful learning signals.
78	
79	    Reference: https://huggingface.co/papers/2511.20347 TRL implementation:
80	    https://github.com/huggingface/trl/blob/1bd2a52ec2d8344050af736d60cdc735181ae4b8/trl/trainer/grpo_trainer.py#L1913
81	
82	    Args:
83	        importance_ratio: The importance sampling ratio (pi_theta / pi_old).
84	        temperature: Temperature parameter controlling the softness of the gate.
85	
86	    Returns:
87	        The SAPO loss value.
88	    """
89	    if temperature <= 0:
90	        raise ValueError("sapo_temperature must be > 0.")
91	    sigmoid_input = temperature * (importance_ratio - 1)
92	    sigmoid_smoothed_loss = torch.sigmoid(sigmoid_input)
93	    return sigmoid_smoothed_loss * 4 / temperature
94	
95	
96	def clip_coef_fn(coef, epsilon_low, epsilon_high, loss_type):
97	    if loss_type == "cispo":
98	        # CISPO: clip and detach the importance weights
99	        upper_bound = epsilon_high
100	        lower_bound = None
101	        clipped_coef = torch.clamp(coef, lower_bound, upper_bound).detach()
102	        is_lower_clipped = False
103	        is_upper_clipped = coef > upper_bound
104	    elif loss_type in ("sapo", "vespo"):
105	        # SAPO / VESPO don't use clipping metrics
106	        clipped_coef = None
107	        is_lower_clipped = torch.zeros_like(coef, dtype=torch.bool)
108	        is_upper_clipped = torch.zeros_like(coef, dtype=torch.bool)
109	    else:
110	        upper_bound = 1 + epsilon_high
111	        lower_bound = 1 - epsilon_low
112	        clipped_coef = torch.clamp(coef, lower_bound, upper_bound)
113	        is_lower_clipped = coef < lower_bound
114	        is_upper_clipped = coef > upper_bound
115	    return clipped_coef, is_lower_clipped, is_upper_clipped

146	        # Validate sequence-level + loss_type combinations

150	                f"Use importance_sampling_level='token' instead."

155	            ref_per_token_logps = per_token_logps.detach()

157	        # Compute policy gradient loss with importance sampling ratio

174	        coef_1 = torch.exp(log_importance_weights)

1414	    def get_high_entropy_mask(self, entropies: torch.Tensor, mask: torch.Tensor, threshold: float) -> torch.Tensor:
1415	        """
1416	        Returns a binary mask identifying tokens whose entropy exceeds a given quantile threshold.
1417	
1418	        Args:
1419	            entropies (`torch.Tensor`):
1420	                Tensor of shape (batch_size, seq_len) with per-token entropy values.
1421	            mask (`torch.Tensor`):
1422	                Binary mask of the same shape as `entropies`, where `1` indicates valid tokens and `0` padding.
1423	            threshold (`float`):
1424	                Quantile threshold between `0.0` and `1.0` to select high-entropy tokens.
1425	
1426	        Returns:
1427	            `torch.Tensor`:
1428	                Boolean mask of shape (batch_size, seq_len), where `True` indicates tokens with entropy >= threshold
1429	                and `False` otherwise.
1430	        """
1431	        local = entropies[mask.bool()].float()
1432	
1433	        # Use a negative pad_value as a sentinel because entropy values are always >= 0.
1434	        # This guarantees that the sentinel cannot collide with any real entropy value.
1435	        pad_value = -1e9
1436	
1437	        # Pad across processes so that every rank has the same tensor length
1438	        padded = self.accelerator.pad_across_processes(local, dim=0, pad_index=pad_value)
1439	        gathered = self.accelerator.gather(padded)
1440	
1441	        # Drop sentinel values (safe because no entropy can be negative)
1442	        gathered = gathered[gathered != pad_value]
1443	
1444	        if gathered.numel() == 0:
1445	            return torch.zeros_like(entropies, dtype=torch.bool)
1446	
1447	        entropy_threshold = torch.quantile(gathered, threshold)
1448	        masked_entropies = entropies * mask.float()
1449	        entropy_mask = masked_entropies >= entropy_threshold
1450	        return entropy_mask & mask.bool()  # ensure padding tokens are always masked out

3039	    def get_off_policy_mask(
3040	        advantages: torch.Tensor,
3041	        per_token_logps: torch.Tensor,
3042	        sampling_per_token_logps: torch.Tensor,
3043	        mask: torch.Tensor,
3044	        off_policy_threshold: float,
3045	    ) -> torch.Tensor:

3048	        "Keep" and 0.0 indicates "Drop".
3049	        """
3050	        # forward KL div: log(pi_old) - log(pi_theta)
3051	        kl_div = sampling_per_token_logps - per_token_logps.detach()
3052	        # Tokens vLLM could not score carry NaN and provide no KL evidence. Left in, the sequence mean is NaN,

3054	        # on the strength of a single unscorable token.
3055	        kl_div = torch.nan_to_num(kl_div, nan=0.0)

3057	        seq_kl_sum = (kl_div * mask).sum(dim=1, keepdim=True)
3058	        avg_seq_kl = seq_kl_sum / mask.sum(dim=1, keepdim=True).clamp(min=1.0)
3059	        # Keep if (Advantage >= 0) OR (KL <= delta)
3060	        is_pos_adv = advantages >= 0
3061	        is_low_kl = avg_seq_kl <= off_policy_threshold

3066	    def get_gamma_weights(
3067	        advantages: torch.Tensor,
3068	        log_ratio_per_token: torch.Tensor,
3069	        mask: torch.Tensor,
3070	        importance_sampling_ratio: torch.Tensor | None,  # (B, T)
3071	        k_pos: float = 2.0,
3072	        lambda_pos: float = 3.0,
3073	        k_neg: float = 3.0,
3074	        lambda_neg: float = 2.0,
3075	    ) -> torch.Tensor:
3076	        """
3077	        Computes the Gamma weights for the VESPO loss. For reference:
3078	            φ(w) = e^λ × w^k × e^{-λw} is the gamma weighting (normalized so φ(1)=1)
3079	                with w = sequence-level importance sampling ratio
3080	        note: we will compute φ(w) in log space
3081	
3082	        φ(w) is detached via @torch.no_grad(), only acts as gradient scaling coefficient
3083	
3084	        VESPO loss = -φ(w) × A × log_prob, gradient naturally gives φ(w) × A × ∇log π
3085	        """

3087	        # This is solely for matching truthfully the original implementation, otherwise keeping -20 could be fine.
3088	        lower_clamp = math.log(1e-8)
3089	
3090	        # Sequence-level log ratio Σ log(π_θ/π_old) (not a mean like for `log_importance_weights`)
3091	        log_ratio_clamped = torch.clamp(log_ratio_per_token, -20.0, 20.0)
3092	        seq_log_ratio = torch.sum(log_ratio_clamped * mask, dim=-1, keepdim=True)  # (B, 1)
3093	
3094	        # Apply token-level TIS or MIS correction (in log space)
3095	        if importance_sampling_ratio is not None:
3096	            log_is_ratio = torch.clamp(torch.log(importance_sampling_ratio), lower_clamp, 20.0)
3097	            # log(w) = log(π_θ/π_old) + log(π_old/π_sampler)
3098	            seq_log_ratio += torch.sum(log_is_ratio, dim=-1, keepdim=True)
3099	
3100	        log_w_seq = torch.clamp(seq_log_ratio, lower_clamp, 20.0)
3101	        w_seq = torch.exp(log_w_seq)
3102	
3103	        # compute k and lambda based on advantage sign
3104	        is_nonneg_adv = advantages >= 0
3105	        k_seq = torch.where(is_nonneg_adv, k_pos, k_neg)
3106	        lambda_seq = torch.where(is_nonneg_adv, lambda_pos, lambda_neg).clamp(min=1e-4)
3107	
3108	        # log(φ(w)) = λ + k × log(w) - λ × w
3109	        log_phi = lambda_seq + k_seq * log_w_seq - lambda_seq * w_seq
3110	        phi_seq = torch.exp(log_phi).nan_to_num(nan=0.0, posinf=0.0, neginf=0.0)
3111	
3112	        return phi_seq  # (B, 1)

16	def number(text):
17	    match = re.search(r"(?:####\s*|\\boxed\{)([-+]?\d[\d,]*(?:\.\d+)?)", text)

21	class RecordMetrics(TrainerCallback):
22	    def __init__(self, directory):
23	        self.path = directory / f"metrics_rank{int(os.environ.get('RANK', 0))}.jsonl"
24	
25	    def on_log(self, args, state, control, logs=None, **kwargs):
26	        with self.path.open("a") as stream:
27	            stream.write(json.dumps({"step": state.global_step, **logs}) + "\n")

30	class RecordedGRPO(GRPOTrainer):
31	    def __init__(self, *args, record_directory, record_tokens, **kwargs):
32	        self.record_directory = record_directory
33	        self.record_tokens = record_tokens
34	        self.record_index = 0
35	        self.capture_logps = False
36	        super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)
37	
38	    def _get_per_token_logps_and_entropies(self, *args, **kwargs):
39	        result = super()._get_per_token_logps_and_entropies(*args, **kwargs)
40	        if self.capture_logps:
41	            self.recorded_logps = result[0].detach()
42	        return result
43	
44	    def _compute_loss(self, model, inputs):
45	        self.capture_logps = self.record_tokens and model.training
46	        loss = super()._compute_loss(model, inputs)
47	        if self.capture_logps:
48	            directory = self.record_directory / "token_records"
49	            directory.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
50	            logps = self.recorded_logps
51	            previous = inputs.get("old_per_token_logps")
52	            previous = logps if previous is None else previous
53	            filename = f"step{self.state.global_step:04d}_batch{self.record_index:05d}_rank{self.accelerator.process_index}.npz"
54	            np.savez_compressed(
55	                directory / filename,
56	                logps=logps.float().cpu().numpy(),
57	                old_logps=previous.detach().float().cpu().numpy(),
58	                advantages=inputs["advantages"].detach().float().cpu().numpy(),
59	                mask=inputs["completion_mask"].detach().cpu().numpy(),
60	                generation_token_count=float(inputs["num_items_in_batch"]),
61	                loss=float(loss.detach()),
62	                accumulation_steps=self.current_gradient_accumulation_steps,
63	                generation_steps=self.args.steps_per_generation,
64	                world_size=self.accelerator.num_processes,
65	                clip_low=self.epsilon_low,
66	                clip_high=self.epsilon_high,
67	            )
68	            self.record_index += 1
69	        self.capture_logps = False
70	        return loss

73	def main():
74	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
75	    parser.add_argument("--model", type=Path, required=True)
76	    parser.add_argument("--data", type=Path, required=True)
77	    parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path, required=True)
78	    parser.add_argument("--case", choices=["tokens", "metrics"], required=True)
79	    parser.add_argument("--steps", type=int, default=24)
80	    parser.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=42)
81	    parser.add_argument("--resume", action="store_true")
82	    args = parser.parse_args()
83	    args.output.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
84	    rank = int(os.environ.get("RANK", 0))
85	    rollout_path = args.output / f"rollouts_rank{rank}.jsonl"
86	    dataset = Dataset.from_parquet(str(args.data / "train.parquet")).shuffle(seed=args.seed).select(range(256))
87	    validation = Dataset.from_parquet(str(args.data / "test.parquet")).select(range(64))
88	
89	    def format_row(row):
90	        return {"prompt": [{"role": "user", "content": row["question"] + "\nSolve the problem and write the final numerical answer after ####."}], "answer": number(row["answer"])}
91	
92	    dataset = dataset.map(format_row, remove_columns=dataset.column_names)
93	    validation = validation.map(format_row, remove_columns=validation.column_names)
94	
95	    def correctness(completions, answer, prompts, log_metric, trainer_state, **kwargs):
96	        texts = [completion[0]["content"] for completion in completions]
97	        parsed = [number(text) for text in texts]
98	        rewards = [float(predicted == expected) for predicted, expected in zip(parsed, answer)]
99	        with rollout_path.open("a") as stream:
100	            for prompt, text, expected, predicted, reward in zip(prompts, texts, answer, parsed, rewards):
101	                stream.write(json.dumps({"step": trainer_state.global_step, "prompt": prompt, "completion": text, "answer": expected, "parsed": predicted, "reward": reward}) + "\n")
102	        if args.case == "metrics" and rank == 0:
103	            log_metric("answer_parse_rate", sum(value is not None for value in parsed) / len(parsed))
104	        return rewards
105	
106	    tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(args.model, local_files_only=True, padding_side="left")
107	    model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(args.model, local_files_only=True, dtype=torch.float32, attn_implementation="sdpa")
108	    configuration = GRPOConfig(
109	        output_dir=str(args.output / "checkpoints"),
110	        run_name=f"gsm8k_{args.case}_seed{args.seed}",
111	        max_steps=args.steps,
112	        seed=args.seed,
113	        data_seed=args.seed,
114	        per_device_train_batch_size=2,
115	        per_device_eval_batch_size=4,
116	        gradient_accumulation_steps=2,
117	        steps_per_generation=4,
118	        num_generations=4,
119	        max_completion_length=256,
120	        temperature=0.8,
121	        learning_rate=1e-6,
122	        lr_scheduler_type="constant",
123	        bf16=True,
124	        beta=0.0,
125	        loss_type="dapo",
126	        scale_rewards="group",
127	        use_vllm=False,
128	        use_liger_kernel=False,
129	        gradient_checkpointing=False,
130	        logging_steps=1,
131	        save_strategy="steps",
132	        save_steps=6,
133	        save_total_limit=1,
134	        eval_strategy="no",
135	        report_to=["wandb"],
136	        ddp_timeout=90,
137	        ddp_find_unused_parameters=False,
138	    )
139	    trainer = RecordedGRPO(
140	        model=model,
141	        processing_class=tokenizer,
142	        args=configuration,
143	        train_dataset=dataset,
144	        eval_dataset=validation,
145	        reward_funcs=correctness,
146	        record_directory=args.output,
147	        record_tokens=args.case == "tokens",
148	        callbacks=[RecordMetrics(args.output)],
149	    )
150	    checkpoint = get_last_checkpoint(str(args.output / "checkpoints")) if args.resume else None
151	    result = trainer.train(resume_from_checkpoint=checkpoint)
152	    trainer.save_state()
153	    metrics = trainer.evaluate()
154	    if trainer.accelerator.is_main_process:
155	        (args.output / "final_metrics.json").write_text(json.dumps({"step": trainer.state.global_step, "training": result.metrics, "evaluation": metrics}, indent=2) + "\n")
156	
157	
158	if __name__ == "__main__":
159	    main()

1421	            mask (`torch.Tensor`):

30	def k3_loss_fn(log_p, log_q):
31	    # computes k3 estimate of KL[q, p]
32	    # ref: http://joschu.net/blog/kl-approx.html
33	    return torch.exp(log_p - log_q) - (log_p - log_q) - 1.0

36	@torch.no_grad()
37	def get_gamma_weights(
38	    advantages: torch.Tensor,
39	    log_ratio_per_token: torch.Tensor,
40	    mask: torch.Tensor,
41	    importance_sampling_ratio: torch.Tensor | None = None,
42	    k_pos: float = 2.0,
43	    lambda_pos: float = 3.0,
44	    k_neg: float = 3.0,
45	    lambda_neg: float = 2.0,
46	) -> torch.Tensor:
47	    """VESPO gamma weighting: phi(w) = e^lambda * w^k * e^{-lambda*w} (normalized so phi(1)=1).
48	
49	    Computed in log space and detached (via ``@torch.no_grad``) so ``phi_seq`` acts purely as a gradient-scaling
50	    coefficient. Returns a (B, 1) tensor. TRL reference: ``trl.trainer.grpo_trainer.GRPOTrainer.get_gamma_weights``.
51	    """
52	    lower_clamp = math.log(1e-8)
53	
54	    log_ratio_clamped = torch.clamp(log_ratio_per_token, -20.0, 20.0)
55	    seq_log_ratio = torch.sum(log_ratio_clamped * mask, dim=-1, keepdim=True)  # (B, 1)
56	
57	    if importance_sampling_ratio is not None:
58	        log_is_ratio = torch.clamp(torch.log(importance_sampling_ratio), lower_clamp, 20.0)
59	        seq_log_ratio = seq_log_ratio + torch.sum(log_is_ratio, dim=-1, keepdim=True)
60	
61	    log_w_seq = torch.clamp(seq_log_ratio, lower_clamp, 20.0)
62	    w_seq = torch.exp(log_w_seq)
63	
64	    is_nonneg_adv = advantages.unsqueeze(-1) >= 0
65	    k_seq = torch.where(is_nonneg_adv, k_pos, k_neg)
66	    lambda_seq = torch.where(is_nonneg_adv, lambda_pos, lambda_neg).clamp(min=1e-4)
67	
68	    log_phi = lambda_seq + k_seq * log_w_seq - lambda_seq * w_seq
69	    phi_seq = torch.exp(log_phi).nan_to_num(nan=0.0, posinf=0.0, neginf=0.0)
70	    return phi_seq

73	def sapo_loss_fn(importance_ratio: torch.Tensor, temperature: float) -> torch.Tensor:
74	    """SAPO (Soft Adaptive Policy Optimization) loss function.
75	
76	    Replaces hard clipping with a smooth, temperature-controlled gate that adaptively attenuates off-policy updates
77	    while preserving useful learning signals.
78	
79	    Reference: https://huggingface.co/papers/2511.20347 TRL implementation:
80	    https://github.com/huggingface/trl/blob/1bd2a52ec2d8344050af736d60cdc735181ae4b8/trl/trainer/grpo_trainer.py#L1913
81	
82	    Args:
83	        importance_ratio: The importance sampling ratio (pi_theta / pi_old).
84	        temperature: Temperature parameter controlling the softness of the gate.
85	
86	    Returns:
87	        The SAPO loss value.
88	    """
89	    if temperature <= 0:
90	        raise ValueError("sapo_temperature must be > 0.")
91	    sigmoid_input = temperature * (importance_ratio - 1)
92	    sigmoid_smoothed_loss = torch.sigmoid(sigmoid_input)
93	    return sigmoid_smoothed_loss * 4 / temperature

96	def clip_coef_fn(coef, epsilon_low, epsilon_high, loss_type):
97	    if loss_type == "cispo":
98	        # CISPO: clip and detach the importance weights
99	        upper_bound = epsilon_high
100	        lower_bound = None
101	        clipped_coef = torch.clamp(coef, lower_bound, upper_bound).detach()
102	        is_lower_clipped = False
103	        is_upper_clipped = coef > upper_bound
104	    elif loss_type in ("sapo", "vespo"):
105	        # SAPO / VESPO don't use clipping metrics
106	        clipped_coef = None
107	        is_lower_clipped = torch.zeros_like(coef, dtype=torch.bool)
108	        is_upper_clipped = torch.zeros_like(coef, dtype=torch.bool)
109	    else:
110	        upper_bound = 1 + epsilon_high
111	        lower_bound = 1 - epsilon_low
112	        clipped_coef = torch.clamp(coef, lower_bound, upper_bound)
113	        is_lower_clipped = coef < lower_bound
114	        is_upper_clipped = coef > upper_bound
115	    return clipped_coef, is_lower_clipped, is_upper_clipped

1261	
1262	        # In the following figure, the values are the prompt indices. Each row shows the per-step batch

1267	        #                                      |   GPU 0  |   GPU 1  |

1270	        #                                       <-───────> per_device_train_batch_size=3
1271	        #  grad_accum    ▲  ▲  0          0     0   0   1   1   2   2   <- Generate for the first `steps_per_generation` (prompts 0 to 11); store the completions; use the first slice to compute the loss

1253	    def _get_train_sampler(self, dataset: Dataset | None = None) -> Sampler:
1254	        # Returns a sampler that
1255	        # 1. ensures each prompt is repeated across multiple processes. This guarantees that identical prompts are
1256	        #    distributed to different GPUs, allowing rewards to be computed and normalized correctly within each prompt
1257	        #    group. Using the same seed across processes ensures consistent prompt assignment, preventing discrepancies
1258	        #    in group formation.
1259	        # 2. repeats the batch multiple times to allow reusing generations across multiple updates. Refer to
1260	        #    _prepare_inputs to see how the generations are stored and reused.
1261	
1262	        # In the following figure, the values are the prompt indices. Each row shows the per-step batch
1263	        # returned by `_prepare_inputs`; rows within a `steps_per_generation` block are slices of the same
1264	        # generated batch. When `num_iterations > 1`, that block is reused for multiple optimization passes
1265	        # before regenerating.
1266	        #
1267	        #                                      |   GPU 0  |   GPU 1  |
1268	        #
1269	        #                 global_step   step    <-───>  num_generations=2
1270	        #                                       <-───────> per_device_train_batch_size=3
1271	        #  grad_accum    ▲  ▲  0          0     0   0   1   1   2   2   <- Generate for the first `steps_per_generation` (prompts 0 to 11); store the completions; use the first slice to compute the loss
1272	        #     =2         ▼  |  0          1     3   3   4   4   5   5   <- Take the stored generations and use the second slice to compute the loss
1273	        #                   |
1274	        #                   |  1          2     6   6   7   7   8   8   <- Take the stored generations and use the third slice to compute the loss
1275	        #  steps_per_gen=4  ▼  1          3     9   9  10  10  11  11   <- Take the stored generations and use the fourth slice to compute the loss
1276	        #
1277	        #                      2          4    12  12  13  13  14  14   <- Generate for the second `steps_per_generation` (prompts 12 to 23); store the completions; use the first slice to compute the loss
1278	        #                      2          5    15  15  16  16  17  17   <- Take the stored generations and use the second slice to compute the loss
1279	        #                                          ...
1280	        if dataset is None:
1281	            dataset = self.train_dataset
1282	        return RepeatSampler(
1283	            data_source=dataset,
1284	            mini_repeat_count=self.num_generations,
1285	            batch_size=self.args.generation_batch_size // self.num_generations,
1286	            repeat_count=self.num_iterations * self.args.steps_per_generation,

1414	    def get_high_entropy_mask(self, entropies: torch.Tensor, mask: torch.Tensor, threshold: float) -> torch.Tensor:
1415	        """
1416	        Returns a binary mask identifying tokens whose entropy exceeds a given quantile threshold.
1417	
1418	        Args:
1419	            entropies (`torch.Tensor`):
1420	                Tensor of shape (batch_size, seq_len) with per-token entropy values.
1421	            mask (`torch.Tensor`):
1422	                Binary mask of the same shape as `entropies`, where `1` indicates valid tokens and `0` padding.
1423	            threshold (`float`):
1424	                Quantile threshold between `0.0` and `1.0` to select high-entropy tokens.
1425	
1426	        Returns:
1427	            `torch.Tensor`:
1428	                Boolean mask of shape (batch_size, seq_len), where `True` indicates tokens with entropy >= threshold
1429	                and `False` otherwise.
1430	        """
1431	        local = entropies[mask.bool()].float()
1432	
1433	        # Use a negative pad_value as a sentinel because entropy values are always >= 0.
1434	        # This guarantees that the sentinel cannot collide with any real entropy value.
1435	        pad_value = -1e9
1436	
1437	        # Pad across processes so that every rank has the same tensor length
1438	        padded = self.accelerator.pad_across_processes(local, dim=0, pad_index=pad_value)
1439	        gathered = self.accelerator.gather(padded)
1440	
1441	        # Drop sentinel values (safe because no entropy can be negative)
1442	        gathered = gathered[gathered != pad_value]
1443	
1444	        if gathered.numel() == 0:
1445	            return torch.zeros_like(entropies, dtype=torch.bool)
1446	
1447	        entropy_threshold = torch.quantile(gathered, threshold)
1448	        masked_entropies = entropies * mask.float()
1449	        entropy_mask = masked_entropies >= entropy_threshold
1450	        return entropy_mask & mask.bool()  # ensure padding tokens are always masked out

1934	    def _get_tool_suffix_ids(self, tool_messages):
1935	        """Get token IDs for tool result formatting by using a minimal dummy conversation."""

1937	        # header from the assistant's tool call name.
1938	        dummy_tool_calls = [{"type": "function", "function": {"name": tool_messages[0]["name"], "arguments": {}}}]
1939	        dummy_messages = [
1940	            {"role": "user", "content": "dummy"},
1941	            {
1942	                "role": "assistant",
1943	                # "content" is required here because VLM processors crash on tokenize=True without it
1944	                # (KeyError in processing_utils.py). See huggingface/transformers#45290.
1945	                "content": "",
1946	                "tool_calls": dummy_tool_calls,
1947	            },
1948	        ]
1949	        if self._is_vlm:
1950	            dummy_messages = prepare_multimodal_messages(dummy_messages)
1951	            tool_messages = prepare_multimodal_messages(tool_messages)
1952	
1953	        prefix_ids = self.processing_class.apply_chat_template(
1954	            dummy_messages,
1955	            add_generation_prompt=False,
1956	            tokenize=True,
1957	            chat_template=self.chat_template,
1958	            return_dict=False,
1959	            **self.chat_template_kwargs,
1960	        )
1961	        full_ids = self.processing_class.apply_chat_template(
1962	            dummy_messages + tool_messages,
1963	            add_generation_prompt=True,
1964	            tokenize=True,
1965	            chat_template=self.chat_template,
1966	            return_dict=False,
1967	            **self.chat_template_kwargs,
1968	        )

1970	        if self._is_vlm:

1972	            full_ids = full_ids[0]
1973	
1974	        # Some chat templates (notably Qwen3/Qwen3.5) render "...<|im_end|>\n" after an assistant/tool block.
1975	        # When we compute `suffix_ids` by slicing `full_ids`, we must align the slicing boundary to

3038	    @staticmethod
3039	    def get_off_policy_mask(
3040	        advantages: torch.Tensor,
3041	        per_token_logps: torch.Tensor,
3042	        sampling_per_token_logps: torch.Tensor,
3043	        mask: torch.Tensor,
3044	        off_policy_threshold: float,
3045	    ) -> torch.Tensor:
3046	        """

3048	        "Keep" and 0.0 indicates "Drop".
3049	        """
3050	        # forward KL div: log(pi_old) - log(pi_theta)
3051	        kl_div = sampling_per_token_logps - per_token_logps.detach()
3052	        # Tokens vLLM could not score carry NaN and provide no KL evidence. Left in, the sequence mean is NaN,
3053	        # `avg_seq_kl <= off_policy_threshold` is then False, and a negative-advantage sequence would be dropped
3054	        # on the strength of a single unscorable token.
3055	        kl_div = torch.nan_to_num(kl_div, nan=0.0)

3060	        is_pos_adv = advantages >= 0

3064	    @staticmethod
3065	    @torch.no_grad()
3066	    def get_gamma_weights(
3067	        advantages: torch.Tensor,
3068	        log_ratio_per_token: torch.Tensor,
3069	        mask: torch.Tensor,
3070	        importance_sampling_ratio: torch.Tensor | None,  # (B, T)
3071	        k_pos: float = 2.0,
3072	        lambda_pos: float = 3.0,
3073	        k_neg: float = 3.0,
3074	        lambda_neg: float = 2.0,
3075	    ) -> torch.Tensor:
3076	        """
3077	        Computes the Gamma weights for the VESPO loss. For reference:
3078	            φ(w) = e^λ × w^k × e^{-λw} is the gamma weighting (normalized so φ(1)=1)
3079	                with w = sequence-level importance sampling ratio
3080	        note: we will compute φ(w) in log space
3081	
3082	        φ(w) is detached via @torch.no_grad(), only acts as gradient scaling coefficient
3083	
3084	        VESPO loss = -φ(w) × A × log_prob, gradient naturally gives φ(w) × A × ∇log π
3085	        """
3086	        # reducing clamp range directly to log(1e-8) ~ -18.42, to avoid recomputing log_w=log(w.clamp(min=1e-8)) later
3087	        # This is solely for matching truthfully the original implementation, otherwise keeping -20 could be fine.
3088	        lower_clamp = math.log(1e-8)
3089	
3090	        # Sequence-level log ratio Σ log(π_θ/π_old) (not a mean like for `log_importance_weights`)
3091	        log_ratio_clamped = torch.clamp(log_ratio_per_token, -20.0, 20.0)
3092	        seq_log_ratio = torch.sum(log_ratio_clamped * mask, dim=-1, keepdim=True)  # (B, 1)
3093	
3094	        # Apply token-level TIS or MIS correction (in log space)
3095	        if importance_sampling_ratio is not None:
3096	            log_is_ratio = torch.clamp(torch.log(importance_sampling_ratio), lower_clamp, 20.0)
3097	            # log(w) = log(π_θ/π_old) + log(π_old/π_sampler)
3098	            seq_log_ratio += torch.sum(log_is_ratio, dim=-1, keepdim=True)
3099	
3100	        log_w_seq = torch.clamp(seq_log_ratio, lower_clamp, 20.0)
3101	        w_seq = torch.exp(log_w_seq)
3102	
3103	        # compute k and lambda based on advantage sign
3104	        is_nonneg_adv = advantages >= 0
3105	        k_seq = torch.where(is_nonneg_adv, k_pos, k_neg)
3106	        lambda_seq = torch.where(is_nonneg_adv, lambda_pos, lambda_neg).clamp(min=1e-4)
3107	
3108	        # log(φ(w)) = λ + k × log(w) - λ × w
3109	        log_phi = lambda_seq + k_seq * log_w_seq - lambda_seq * w_seq
3110	        phi_seq = torch.exp(log_phi).nan_to_num(nan=0.0, posinf=0.0, neginf=0.0)
3111	
3112	        return phi_seq  # (B, 1)

29	    completions: list[list[dict[str, str]]],
30	    solution: list[str],
31	    log_extra: Callable[[str, list], None] | None = None,
32	    **kwargs,
33	) -> list[float | None]:
34	    r"""
35	    Reward function that checks if the completion matches the ground truth.
36	        - If both gold and prediction are parseable → use math verification.
37	        - If gold is not parseable → return `None` to skip the example.
38	
39	    Args:
40	        completions (`list[list[dict[str, str]]]`):
41	            List of completions to be evaluated. Each completion must be a list of one message, i.e. a dictionary
42	            containing the key `"content"` with the value being the text of the completion.
43	        solution (`list[str]`):
44	            List of the raw-text solutions to the questions/problems/prompts.
45	        log_extra (`callable`, *optional*):
46	            Callable to log extra columns to the completions table, provided automatically by the trainer. Defaults to
47	            `None` to allow calling the function directly outside of a trainer (e.g., for testing).
48	        **kwargs:
49	            Additional keyword arguments. This function does not use them, but they are required in the function
50	            signature to ensure compatibility with trainers like [`GRPOTrainer`].
51	    Example:
52	    ```python
53	    >>> from trl.rewards import accuracy_reward
54	
55	    >>> solutions = [r"\frac{1}{3}", r"\frac{1}{3}"]
56	    >>> completions = [
57	    ...     [{"role": "assistant", "content": r"My answer is \boxed{\frac{1}{3}}"}],
58	    ...     [{"role": "assistant", "content": r"My answer is \boxed{\frac{1}{2}}"}],
59	    ... ]
60	    >>> accuracy_reward(completions, solutions)
61	    [1.0, 0.0]
62	    ```
63	    """
64	    if not is_math_verify_available():
65	        raise ImportError("Please install the `math_verify` package to use accuracy_reward")
66	
67	    contents = [completion[0]["content"] for completion in completions]
68	    rewards = []
69	    gold_parsed_strs = []
70	    answer_parsed_strs = []
71	
72	    # math_verify uses signal.alarm() for timeouts, which only works in the main thread.
73	    # Disable timeouts when running in a non-main thread to avoid ValueError.
74	    is_main_thread = threading.current_thread() is threading.main_thread()
75	    parsing_timeout = None if not is_main_thread else 10
76	    verify_timeout = None if not is_main_thread else 5
77	
78	    # Suppress the "Timeout is disabled" warnings from math_verify when we intentionally disable timeouts
79	    if not is_main_thread:
80	        logging.getLogger("math_verify.parser").setLevel(logging.ERROR)
81	        logging.getLogger("math_verify.grader").setLevel(logging.ERROR)

118	def get_cosine_scaled_reward(
119	    max_len: int,
120	    min_value_wrong: float = -1.0,
121	    max_value_wrong: float = -0.5,
122	    min_value_correct: float = 0.5,
123	    max_value_correct: float = 1.0,
124	) -> Callable:
125	    # docstyle-ignore
126	    r"""
127	    Reward function that scales a correctness reward by the completion length following a cosine schedule, to favor
128	    concise reasoning. Reference: Appendix C.1 of the "Demystifying Long Chain-of-Thought Reasoning" paper
129	    (https://huggingface.co/papers/2502.03373).
130	
131	    Correctness is determined by math verification (as in [`~rewards.accuracy_reward`]), and the length is the number
132	    of completion tokens. The reward interpolates along a cosine schedule between a short-completion and a
133	    long-completion bound:
134	
135	    $$
136	    R_{\text{cosine}}(y) = v_{\min} + \frac{1}{2}(v_{\max} - v_{\min})\left(1 + \cos\left(\frac{|y|}{L_{\max}}\pi\right)\right)
137	    $$
138	
139	    For a **correct** completion, $(v_{\min}, v_{\max}) = (\texttt{min\_value\_correct}, \texttt{max\_value\_correct})$,
140	    so a shorter completion is rewarded more. For a **wrong** completion, the bounds are swapped to
141	    $(v_{\min}, v_{\max}) = (\texttt{max\_value\_wrong}, \texttt{min\_value\_wrong})$, so a shorter completion is
142	    penalized more (a longer wrong completion is penalized less, preserving exploration). When the gold solution is not
143	    parseable, the example is skipped (reward `None`), as in [`~rewards.accuracy_reward`].
144	
145	    Args:
146	        max_len (`int`):
147	            Maximum completion length (in tokens) used to normalize the cosine schedule, $L_{\max}$.
148	        min_value_wrong (`float`, *optional*, defaults to `-1.0`):
149	            Reward of a wrong completion at the shortest length.
150	        max_value_wrong (`float`, *optional*, defaults to `-0.5`):
151	            Reward of a wrong completion at the longest length.
152	        min_value_correct (`float`, *optional*, defaults to `0.5`):
153	            Reward of a correct completion at the longest length.
154	        max_value_correct (`float`, *optional*, defaults to `1.0`):
155	            Reward of a correct completion at the shortest length.
156	
157	    Returns:
158	        `Callable`:
159	            A reward function that takes completions, their solutions and token ids, and returns a list of rewards
160	            (`None` for examples with an unparseable gold solution).
161	
162	    Example:
163	    ```python
164	    >>> from trl.rewards import get_cosine_scaled_reward
165	
166	    >>> cosine_scaled_reward = get_cosine_scaled_reward(max_len=100)
167	    >>> completions = [[{"content": r"\boxed{\frac{1}{3}}"}], [{"content": r"\boxed{\frac{1}{2}}"}]]
168	    >>> solution = [r"\frac{1}{3}", r"\frac{1}{3}"]
169	    >>> completion_ids = [[1] * 50, [1] * 50]  # both completions are 50 tokens, half of max_len
170	    >>> cosine_scaled_reward(completions, solution, completion_ids)
171	    [0.75, -0.75]
172	    ```
173	    """
174	    return _CosineScaledReward(max_len, min_value_wrong, max_value_wrong, min_value_correct, max_value_correct)

177	class _CosineScaledReward:
178	    # Callable class rather than a closure so the reward stays picklable: the async GRPO rollout
179	    # worker forwards reward funcs to a spawned child process, and closures can't be pickled.
180	    __name__ = "cosine_scaled_reward"
181	
182	    def __init__(
183	        self,
184	        max_len: int,
185	        min_value_wrong: float,
186	        max_value_wrong: float,
187	        min_value_correct: float,
188	        max_value_correct: float,
189	    ):
190	        self.max_len = max_len
191	        self.min_value_wrong = min_value_wrong
192	        self.max_value_wrong = max_value_wrong
193	        self.min_value_correct = min_value_correct
194	        self.max_value_correct = max_value_correct
195	
196	    def __call__(
197	        self,
198	        completions: list[list[dict[str, str]]],
199	        solution: list[str],
200	        completion_ids: list[list[int]],
201	        **kwargs,
202	    ) -> list[float | None]:
203	        is_correct = accuracy_reward(completions, solution)
204	        rewards = []
205	        for correct, ids in zip(is_correct, completion_ids, strict=True):
206	            if correct is None:
207	                # Gold solution was not parseable; skip the example, as in accuracy_reward.
208	                rewards.append(None)
209	                continue
210	            # Clamp to 1.0 so completions longer than max_len stay at the long-length bound: cos is periodic, so
211	            # without clamping the schedule would climb back up past max_len and reward very long completions.
212	            progress = min(len(ids) / self.max_len, 1.0)
213	            cosine = math.cos(progress * math.pi)
214	            if correct:
215	                min_value, max_value = self.min_value_correct, self.max_value_correct
216	            else:
217	                # Swap the bounds so that a shorter wrong completion is penalized more than a longer one.
218	                min_value, max_value = self.max_value_wrong, self.min_value_wrong
219	            rewards.append(float(min_value + 0.5 * (max_value - min_value) * (1.0 + cosine)))
220	        return rewards
221

223	def reasoning_accuracy_reward(
224	    completions: list[list[dict[str, str]]],
225	    solution: list[str],
226	    reasoning_delimiters: list[str] | None = None,
227	    log_extra: Callable[[str, list], None] | None = None,
228	    **kwargs,
229	) -> list[float | None]:
230	    r"""
231	    Reward function that removes the reasoning content and checks if the final answer matches the ground truth.
232	        - If both gold and prediction are parseable → use math verification.
233	        - If gold is not parseable → return `None` to skip the example.
234	
235	    Args:
236	        completions (`list[list[dict[str, str]]]`):
237	            List of completions to be evaluated. Each completion must be a list of one message, i.e. a dictionary
238	            containing the key `"content"` with the value being the text of the completion.
239	        solution (`list[str]`):
240	            List of the raw-text solutions to the questions/problems/prompts.
241	        reasoning_delimiters (`list[str]]`, *optional*):
242	            List of strings indicating where the reasoning content ends. The final answer is assumed to be after the
243	            last occurrence of any of these delimiters. If `None`, defaults to `["</think>"]`.
244	        log_extra (`callable`, *optional*):
245	            Callable to log extra columns to the completions table, provided automatically by the trainer. Defaults to
246	            `None` to allow calling the function directly outside of a trainer (e.g., for testing).
247	        **kwargs:
248	            Additional keyword arguments. This function does not use them, but they are required in the function
249	            signature to ensure compatibility with trainers like [`GRPOTrainer`].
250	    Example:
251	        ```python
252	        >>> from trl.rewards import reasoning_accuracy_reward
253	
254	        >>> reasoning_delimiters = ["</think>"]
255	        >>> solutions = [r"\frac{1}{3}", r"\frac{1}{3}", r"\frac{1}{3}"]
256	        >>> completions = [
257	        ...     [
258	        ...         {
259	        ...             "role": "assistant",
260	        ...             "content": r"<think> Reasoning content </think> The final answer is \boxed{\frac{1}{3}}",
261	        ...         }
262	        ...     ],
263	        ...     [
264	        ...         {
265	        ...             "role": "assistant",
266	        ...             "content": r"<think> Reasoning content </think> The final answer is \boxed{\frac{1}{2}}",
267	        ...         }
268	        ...     ],
269	        ...     [
270	        ...         {
271	        ...             "role": "assistant",
272	        ...             "content": r"<think> Reasoning content with partial answers \boxed{\frac{1}{3}} but no final answer",
273	        ...         }
274	        ...     ],
275	        ... ]
276	        >>> reasoning_accuracy_reward(completions, solutions, reasoning_delimiters=reasoning_delimiters)
277	        [1.0, 0.0, 0.0]
278	        ```
279	    """
280	    if not is_math_verify_available():
281	        raise ImportError("Please install the `math_verify` package to use reasoning_accuracy_reward")
282	
283	    if reasoning_delimiters is None:
284	        # Use sensible defaults for majority of reasoning models
285	        reasoning_delimiters = ["</think>"]
286	
287	    rewards = []
288	    contents = [completion[0]["content"] for completion in completions]
289	    gold_parsed_strs = []
290	    answer_parsed_strs = []
291	
292	    # math_verify uses signal.alarm() for timeouts, which only works in the main thread.
293	    # Disable timeouts when running in a non-main thread to avoid ValueError.
294	    is_main_thread = threading.current_thread() is threading.main_thread()
295	    parsing_timeout = None if not is_main_thread else 10
296	    verify_timeout = None if not is_main_thread else 5
297	
298	    # Suppress the "Timeout is disabled" warnings from math_verify when we intentionally disable timeouts
299	    if not is_main_thread:
300	        logging.getLogger("math_verify.parser").setLevel(logging.ERROR)
301	        logging.getLogger("math_verify.grader").setLevel(logging.ERROR)
302	
303	    for content, sol in zip(contents, solution, strict=True):
304	        # Split final answer from reasoning content
305	        is_reasoning_complete = False
306	        for delim in reasoning_delimiters:
307	            if delim in content:
308	                content = content.split(delim)[-1]
309	                is_reasoning_complete = True
310	                break
311	        if not is_reasoning_complete:
312	            # We assign zero reward instead of `None` to penalize incomplete reasoning
313	            rewards.append(0.0)
314	            gold_parsed_strs.append("[incomplete reasoning]")
315	            answer_parsed_strs.append("[incomplete reasoning]")
316	            continue
317	
318	        gold_parsed = parse(sol, parsing_timeout=parsing_timeout)
319	        if len(gold_parsed) != 0:
320	            # We require the answer to be provided in correct latex (no malformed operators)
321	            answer_parsed = parse(
322	                content,
323	                extraction_config=[
324	                    LatexExtractionConfig(
325	                        boxed_match_priority=0,
326	                        normalization_config=NormalizationConfig(
327	                            units=True,
328	                        ),
329	                        try_extract_without_anchor=False,
330	                    )
331	                ],
332	                extraction_mode="first_match",
333	                parsing_timeout=parsing_timeout,
334	            )
335	            reward = float(verify(gold_parsed, answer_parsed, timeout_seconds=verify_timeout))
336	            gold_parsed_strs.append(str(gold_parsed))
337	            answer_parsed_strs.append(str(answer_parsed) if answer_parsed else "[unparseable]")
338	        else:
339	            # If the gold solution cannot be parsed, we assign `None` to skip this example
340	            reward = None
341	            gold_parsed_strs.append("[unparseable]")
342	            answer_parsed_strs.append("[skipped]")
343	        rewards.append(reward)
344	
345	    if log_extra is not None:
346	        log_extra("solution", list(solution))
347	        log_extra("gold_parsed", gold_parsed_strs)
348	        log_extra("answer_parsed", answer_parsed_strs)
349	
350	    return rewards

3038	    @staticmethod
3039	    def get_off_policy_mask(
3040	        advantages: torch.Tensor,
3041	        per_token_logps: torch.Tensor,
3042	        sampling_per_token_logps: torch.Tensor,
3043	        mask: torch.Tensor,
3044	        off_policy_threshold: float,
3045	    ) -> torch.Tensor:

3048	        "Keep" and 0.0 indicates "Drop".
3049	        """
3050	        # forward KL div: log(pi_old) - log(pi_theta)
3051	        kl_div = sampling_per_token_logps - per_token_logps.detach()
3052	        # Tokens vLLM could not score carry NaN and provide no KL evidence. Left in, the sequence mean is NaN,
3053	        # `avg_seq_kl <= off_policy_threshold` is then False, and a negative-advantage sequence would be dropped
3054	        # on the strength of a single unscorable token.
3055	        kl_div = torch.nan_to_num(kl_div, nan=0.0)

3058	        avg_seq_kl = seq_kl_sum / mask.sum(dim=1, keepdim=True).clamp(min=1.0)

3060	        is_pos_adv = advantages >= 0

3064	    @staticmethod
3065	    @torch.no_grad()
3066	    def get_gamma_weights(
3067	        advantages: torch.Tensor,
3068	        log_ratio_per_token: torch.Tensor,
3069	        mask: torch.Tensor,
3070	        importance_sampling_ratio: torch.Tensor | None,  # (B, T)
3071	        k_pos: float = 2.0,
3072	        lambda_pos: float = 3.0,
3073	        k_neg: float = 3.0,
3074	        lambda_neg: float = 2.0,
3075	    ) -> torch.Tensor:
3076	        """
3077	        Computes the Gamma weights for the VESPO loss. For reference:
3078	            φ(w) = e^λ × w^k × e^{-λw} is the gamma weighting (normalized so φ(1)=1)
3079	                with w = sequence-level importance sampling ratio
3080	        note: we will compute φ(w) in log space
3081	
3082	        φ(w) is detached via @torch.no_grad(), only acts as gradient scaling coefficient
3083	
3084	        VESPO loss = -φ(w) × A × log_prob, gradient naturally gives φ(w) × A × ∇log π
3085	        """
3086	        # reducing clamp range directly to log(1e-8) ~ -18.42, to avoid recomputing log_w=log(w.clamp(min=1e-8)) later
3087	        # This is solely for matching truthfully the original implementation, otherwise keeping -20 could be fine.
3088	        lower_clamp = math.log(1e-8)
3089	
3090	        # Sequence-level log ratio Σ log(π_θ/π_old) (not a mean like for `log_importance_weights`)
3091	        log_ratio_clamped = torch.clamp(log_ratio_per_token, -20.0, 20.0)
3092	        seq_log_ratio = torch.sum(log_ratio_clamped * mask, dim=-1, keepdim=True)  # (B, 1)
3093	
3094	        # Apply token-level TIS or MIS correction (in log space)
3095	        if importance_sampling_ratio is not None:
3096	            log_is_ratio = torch.clamp(torch.log(importance_sampling_ratio), lower_clamp, 20.0)
3097	            # log(w) = log(π_θ/π_old) + log(π_old/π_sampler)
3098	            seq_log_ratio += torch.sum(log_is_ratio, dim=-1, keepdim=True)
3099	
3100	        log_w_seq = torch.clamp(seq_log_ratio, lower_clamp, 20.0)
3101	        w_seq = torch.exp(log_w_seq)
3102	
3103	        # compute k and lambda based on advantage sign
3104	        is_nonneg_adv = advantages >= 0
3105	        k_seq = torch.where(is_nonneg_adv, k_pos, k_neg)
3106	        lambda_seq = torch.where(is_nonneg_adv, lambda_pos, lambda_neg).clamp(min=1e-4)
3107	
3108	        # log(φ(w)) = λ + k × log(w) - λ × w
3109	        log_phi = lambda_seq + k_seq * log_w_seq - lambda_seq * w_seq
3110	        phi_seq = torch.exp(log_phi).nan_to_num(nan=0.0, posinf=0.0, neginf=0.0)
3111	
3112	        return phi_seq  # (B, 1)

30	def k3_loss_fn(log_p, log_q):
31	    # computes k3 estimate of KL[q, p]
32	    # ref: http://joschu.net/blog/kl-approx.html
33	    return torch.exp(log_p - log_q) - (log_p - log_q) - 1.0

38	    advantages: torch.Tensor,

48	
49	    Computed in log space and detached (via ``@torch.no_grad``) so ``phi_seq`` acts purely as a gradient-scaling
50	    coefficient. Returns a (B, 1) tensor. TRL reference: ``trl.trainer.grpo_trainer.GRPOTrainer.get_gamma_weights``.
51	    """
52	    lower_clamp = math.log(1e-8)
53	
54	    log_ratio_clamped = torch.clamp(log_ratio_per_token, -20.0, 20.0)
55	    seq_log_ratio = torch.sum(log_ratio_clamped * mask, dim=-1, keepdim=True)  # (B, 1)
56	
57	    if importance_sampling_ratio is not None:
58	        log_is_ratio = torch.clamp(torch.log(importance_sampling_ratio), lower_clamp, 20.0)
59	        seq_log_ratio = seq_log_ratio + torch.sum(log_is_ratio, dim=-1, keepdim=True)
60	
61	    log_w_seq = torch.clamp(seq_log_ratio, lower_clamp, 20.0)
62	    w_seq = torch.exp(log_w_seq)
63	
64	    is_nonneg_adv = advantages.unsqueeze(-1) >= 0
65	    k_seq = torch.where(is_nonneg_adv, k_pos, k_neg)
66	    lambda_seq = torch.where(is_nonneg_adv, lambda_pos, lambda_neg).clamp(min=1e-4)
67	
68	    log_phi = lambda_seq + k_seq * log_w_seq - lambda_seq * w_seq
69	    phi_seq = torch.exp(log_phi).nan_to_num(nan=0.0, posinf=0.0, neginf=0.0)
70	    return phi_seq

73	def sapo_loss_fn(importance_ratio: torch.Tensor, temperature: float) -> torch.Tensor:
74	    """SAPO (Soft Adaptive Policy Optimization) loss function.
75	
76	    Replaces hard clipping with a smooth, temperature-controlled gate that adaptively attenuates off-policy updates
77	    while preserving useful learning signals.
78	
79	    Reference: https://huggingface.co/papers/2511.20347 TRL implementation:
80	    https://github.com/huggingface/trl/blob/1bd2a52ec2d8344050af736d60cdc735181ae4b8/trl/trainer/grpo_trainer.py#L1913
81	
82	    Args:
83	        importance_ratio: The importance sampling ratio (pi_theta / pi_old).
84	        temperature: Temperature parameter controlling the softness of the gate.
85	
86	    Returns:
87	        The SAPO loss value.
88	    """
89	    if temperature <= 0:
90	        raise ValueError("sapo_temperature must be > 0.")
91	    sigmoid_input = temperature * (importance_ratio - 1)
92	    sigmoid_smoothed_loss = torch.sigmoid(sigmoid_input)
93	    return sigmoid_smoothed_loss * 4 / temperature
94

96	def clip_coef_fn(coef, epsilon_low, epsilon_high, loss_type):
97	    if loss_type == "cispo":
98	        # CISPO: clip and detach the importance weights
99	        upper_bound = epsilon_high
100	        lower_bound = None
101	        clipped_coef = torch.clamp(coef, lower_bound, upper_bound).detach()
102	        is_lower_clipped = False
103	        is_upper_clipped = coef > upper_bound
104	    elif loss_type in ("sapo", "vespo"):
105	        # SAPO / VESPO don't use clipping metrics
106	        clipped_coef = None
107	        is_lower_clipped = torch.zeros_like(coef, dtype=torch.bool)
108	        is_upper_clipped = torch.zeros_like(coef, dtype=torch.bool)
109	    else:
110	        upper_bound = 1 + epsilon_high
111	        lower_bound = 1 - epsilon_low
112	        clipped_coef = torch.clamp(coef, lower_bound, upper_bound)
113	        is_lower_clipped = coef < lower_bound
114	        is_upper_clipped = coef > upper_bound
115	    return clipped_coef, is_lower_clipped, is_upper_clipped
