118	class FusedLinearGRPOFunction(FusedLinearPPOBase):
119	    @staticmethod
120	    def ppo_loss_fn(
121	        per_token_logps,
122	        attention_mask,
123	        advantages,
124	        full_attention_mask,
125	        ref_per_token_logps=None,  # shape: [chunk_size, seq_len]
126	        old_per_token_logps=None,
127	        epsilon_low=0.2,
128	        epsilon_high=0.2,
129	        beta=0.04,
130	        loss_type="dapo",  # ["grpo", "bnpo", "dr_grpo", "dapo", "cispo", "sapo", "luspo", "vespo"]
131	        max_completion_length=None,  # Required for dr_grpo
132	        importance_sampling_level="token",  # ["token", "sequence"] - new parameter for GSPO
133	        sapo_temperature_pos=1.0,  # Temperature for positive advantages in SAPO
134	        sapo_temperature_neg=1.05,  # Temperature for negative advantages in SAPO
135	        vllm_is_ratio=None,  # vLLM importance sampling ratio (chunk_size, seq_len) or (chunk_size, 1) or None
136	        delta=None,  # Upper clamp for two-sided clipping (INTELLECT-2)
137	        use_bias_correction_kl=False,  # Importance-sampling-corrected KL (DeepSeek-V3.2)
138	        vespo_k_pos=2.0,  # VESPO gamma shape k for non-negative advantages
139	        vespo_lambda_pos=3.0,  # VESPO gamma rate lambda for non-negative advantages
140	        vespo_k_neg=3.0,  # VESPO gamma shape k for negative advantages
141	        vespo_lambda_neg=2.0,  # VESPO gamma rate lambda for negative advantages
142	        num_items_in_batch=None,  # Total active tokens across the entire generation batch (TRL-compat)
143	        **kwargs,
144	    ):
145	        """GRPO Loss Function matching GRPOTrainer implementation."""
146	        # Validate sequence-level + loss_type combinations
147	        if importance_sampling_level == "sequence" and loss_type in ("cispo", "sapo", "vespo"):
148	            raise ValueError(
149	                f"Sequence-level importance sampling is not supported for loss_type='{loss_type}'. "
150	                f"Use importance_sampling_level='token' instead."
151	            )
152	
153	        # Get reference model probabilities
154	        if ref_per_token_logps is None:
155	            ref_per_token_logps = per_token_logps.detach()
156	
157	        # Compute policy gradient loss with importance sampling ratio
158	        old_per_token_logps = old_per_token_logps if old_per_token_logps is not None else per_token_logps.detach()
159	        log_ratio = per_token_logps - old_per_token_logps
160	
161	        if importance_sampling_level == "token":
162	            log_importance_weights = log_ratio
163	        elif importance_sampling_level == "sequence":
164	            log_importance_weights = (log_ratio * attention_mask).sum(-1) / attention_mask.sum(-1).clamp(min=1.0)
165	            log_importance_weights = log_importance_weights.unsqueeze(-1)
166	        else:
167	            raise ValueError(
168	                f"Unknown importance sampling level: {importance_sampling_level}. Possible values are 'token' "
169	                "and 'sequence'."
170	            )
171	
172	        # From here, log_importance_weights (and all subsequent tensors, coef_1, coef_2, etc.) shape depends on
173	        # importance_sampling_level: "token" level: (B, T); "sequence" level: (B, 1)
174	        coef_1 = torch.exp(log_importance_weights)
175	        coef_2, is_lower_clipped, is_upper_clipped = clip_coef_fn(coef_1, epsilon_low, epsilon_high, loss_type)
176	        if loss_type == "cispo":
177	            # CISPO: clip and detach the importance weights, multiply by log probs
178	            # Reference: https://github.com/huggingface/trl/blob/035c3ff151b953ca72cdfe0ee966bc1469a26fde/trl/trainer/grpo_trainer.py#L2030
179	            per_token_loss = -coef_2 * advantages.unsqueeze(1) * per_token_logps
180	        elif loss_type == "sapo":
181	            # SAPO: Soft Adaptive Policy Optimization
182	            # Uses sigmoid-based soft gating instead of hard clipping
183	            # Reference: https://huggingface.co/papers/2511.20347
184	            # TRL implementation: https://github.com/huggingface/trl/blob/1bd2a52ec2d8344050af736d60cdc735181ae4b8/trl/trainer/grpo_trainer.py#L2037-L2046
185	            advantages_expanded = advantages.unsqueeze(1).expand_as(coef_1)
186	            positive_advantages_mask = advantages_expanded > 0
187	
188	            # torch.where over both branches rather than boolean-mask assignment:
189	            # mask indexing lowers to aten.nonzero, which graph-breaks under
190	            # torch.compile. sapo_loss_fn is elementwise so this is identical.
191	            per_token_loss = torch.where(
192	                positive_advantages_mask,
193	                sapo_loss_fn(coef_1, sapo_temperature_pos),
194	                sapo_loss_fn(coef_1, sapo_temperature_neg),
195	            )
196	            per_token_loss = -per_token_loss * advantages_expanded
197	        elif loss_type == "vespo":
198	            # VESPO: Value-Enhanced Sequence-level Policy Optimization.
199	            # Uses a detached gamma weighting phi(w) as a gradient scaling coefficient.
200	            # Reference: TRL grpo_trainer.get_gamma_weights. The vllm correction for
201	            # distribution mismatch is folded into phi_seq via ``importance_sampling_ratio``
202	            # rather than multiplying per_token_loss.
203	            phi_seq = get_gamma_weights(
204	                advantages=advantages,
205	                log_ratio_per_token=log_ratio,
206	                mask=attention_mask,
207	                importance_sampling_ratio=vllm_is_ratio,
208	                k_pos=vespo_k_pos,
209	                lambda_pos=vespo_lambda_pos,
210	                k_neg=vespo_k_neg,
211	                lambda_neg=vespo_lambda_neg,
212	            )
213	            per_token_loss = -phi_seq * advantages.unsqueeze(1) * per_token_logps
214	        else:
215	            # Apply delta (two-sided clipping from INTELLECT-2) to coef_1
216	            if delta is not None:
217	                coef_1 = torch.clamp(coef_1, max=delta)
218	            per_token_loss1 = coef_1 * advantages.unsqueeze(1)
219	            per_token_loss2 = coef_2 * advantages.unsqueeze(1)
220	            per_token_loss = -torch.min(per_token_loss1, per_token_loss2)
221	
222	        # Apply vLLM importance sampling correction BEFORE adding KL penalty
223	        # VESPO folds this correction into phi_seq (in log space), so we skip it here.
224	        if vllm_is_ratio is not None and loss_type != "vespo":
225	            per_token_loss = per_token_loss * vllm_is_ratio
226	
227	        if beta != 0.0:
228	            # Compute KL penalty (approximates KL[per_token_logps, ref_per_token_logps])
229	            kl_div = k3_loss_fn(ref_per_token_logps, per_token_logps)
230	            if use_bias_correction_kl:
231	                # Importance-sampling-corrected KL (DeepSeek-V3.2): kl *= coef_1.
232	                # Use exp(log_importance_weights) so the ratio's shape matches
233	                # importance_sampling_level (token: (B, T); sequence: (B, 1)),
234	                # mirroring TRL's ``per_token_kl * coef_1`` (un-clamped, before delta).
235	                kl_div = kl_div * torch.exp(log_importance_weights)
236	            # Combine losses
237	            per_token_loss = per_token_loss + beta * kl_div
238	
239	        # Note: We normalize by the number of tokens in the batch (using full_attention_mask),
240	        # which is consistent with the DAPO loss implementation (https://arxiv.org/html/2503.14476v1)
241	        # and TRL GRPO implementation
242	        # (https://github.com/huggingface/trl/blob/e751a16df56e70190fb94bed4a2035eec3303777/trl/trainer/grpo_trainer.py#L966)
243	        if loss_type == "grpo" or loss_type == "sapo":
244	            # Average per-sequence loss (SAPO uses same normalization as GRPO)
245	            loss = (
246	                (per_token_loss * attention_mask).sum(-1) / torch.clamp(attention_mask.sum(-1), min=1.0)
247	            ).sum() / full_attention_mask.shape[0]
248	        elif loss_type == "bnpo":
249	            # Batch Normalized Per-token loss (original implementation)
250	            loss = (per_token_loss * attention_mask).sum() / torch.clamp(full_attention_mask.sum(), min=1.0)
251	        elif loss_type == "dr_grpo":
252	            # Dimension-Reduced GRPO (normalize by batch_size * max_completion_length)
253	            if max_completion_length is None:
254	                raise ValueError("max_completion_length must be provided for loss_type 'dr_grpo'")
255	            loss = (per_token_loss * attention_mask).sum() / (full_attention_mask.shape[0] * max_completion_length)
256	        elif loss_type in ("dapo", "cispo", "vespo"):
257	            loss_normalizer = FusedLinearPPOBase._compute_dapo_normalizer(
258	                full_attention_mask, num_items_in_batch=num_items_in_batch
259	            )
260	            loss = (per_token_loss * attention_mask).sum() / loss_normalizer
261	        elif loss_type == "luspo":
262	            # Match TRL exactly: loss = (per_token_loss * mask.sum(1, keepdim=True)).mean()
263	            weighted = per_token_loss * attention_mask.sum(1, keepdim=True)
264	            loss = weighted.sum() / (full_attention_mask.shape[0] * weighted.shape[1])
265	        else:
266	            raise ValueError(f"Unknown loss type: {loss_type}")
267	
268	        # Calculate metrics
269	        metrics = []
270	        if beta != 0.0:
271	            metrics.append((kl_div * attention_mask).sum() / torch.clamp(full_attention_mask.sum(), min=1.0))
272	
273	        # Adjust clipping metric calculation based on importance sampling level
274	        if importance_sampling_level == "token":
275	            is_clipped = (is_lower_clipped & (advantages.unsqueeze(1) < 0)) | (
276	                is_upper_clipped & (advantages.unsqueeze(1) > 0)
277	            )
278	        else:  # sequence level
279	            # For sequence level, coef_1 is shape (B, 1), advantages is shape (B,)
280	            is_clipped = (is_lower_clipped & (advantages.unsqueeze(1) < 0)) | (
281	                is_upper_clipped & (advantages.unsqueeze(1) > 0)
282	            )
283	            is_clipped = is_clipped.expand_as(attention_mask)
284	
285	        metrics.append((is_clipped * attention_mask).sum() / torch.clamp(full_attention_mask.sum(), min=1.0))
286	        return loss, metrics

1228	    # efficient. Thus, `_prepare_inputs` is called with this *generation* batch, and it handles the splitting internally.

1253	    def _get_train_sampler(self, dataset: Dataset | None = None) -> Sampler:
1254	        # Returns a sampler that
1255	        # 1. ensures each prompt is repeated across multiple processes. This guarantees that identical prompts are
1256	        #    distributed to different GPUs, allowing rewards to be computed and normalized correctly within each prompt
1257	        #    group. Using the same seed across processes ensures consistent prompt assignment, preventing discrepancies
1258	        #    in group formation.
1259	        # 2. repeats the batch multiple times to allow reusing generations across multiple updates. Refer to
1260	        #    _prepare_inputs to see how the generations are stored and reused.
1261	
1262	        # In the following figure, the values are the prompt indices. Each row shows the per-step batch
1263	        # returned by `_prepare_inputs`; rows within a `steps_per_generation` block are slices of the same
1264	        # generated batch. When `num_iterations > 1`, that block is reused for multiple optimization passes
1265	        # before regenerating.
1266	        #
1267	        #                                      |   GPU 0  |   GPU 1  |
1268	        #
1269	        #                 global_step   step    <-───>  num_generations=2
1270	        #                                       <-───────> per_device_train_batch_size=3
1271	        #  grad_accum    ▲  ▲  0          0     0   0   1   1   2   2   <- Generate for the first `steps_per_generation` (prompts 0 to 11); store the completions; use the first slice to compute the loss
1272	        #     =2         ▼  |  0          1     3   3   4   4   5   5   <- Take the stored generations and use the second slice to compute the loss
1273	        #                   |
1274	        #                   |  1          2     6   6   7   7   8   8   <- Take the stored generations and use the third slice to compute the loss
1275	        #  steps_per_gen=4  ▼  1          3     9   9  10  10  11  11   <- Take the stored generations and use the fourth slice to compute the loss
1276	        #
1277	        #                      2          4    12  12  13  13  14  14   <- Generate for the second `steps_per_generation` (prompts 12 to 23); store the completions; use the first slice to compute the loss
1278	        #                      2          5    15  15  16  16  17  17   <- Take the stored generations and use the second slice to compute the loss
1279	        #                                          ...
1280	        if dataset is None:
1281	            dataset = self.train_dataset
1282	        return RepeatSampler(
1283	            data_source=dataset,
1284	            mini_repeat_count=self.num_generations,
1285	            batch_size=self.args.generation_batch_size // self.num_generations,
1286	            repeat_count=self.num_iterations * self.args.steps_per_generation,
1287	            shuffle=self.shuffle_dataset,
1288	            seed=self.args.seed,
1289	        )
1290

1414	    def get_high_entropy_mask(self, entropies: torch.Tensor, mask: torch.Tensor, threshold: float) -> torch.Tensor:
1415	        """
1416	        Returns a binary mask identifying tokens whose entropy exceeds a given quantile threshold.
1417	
1418	        Args:
1419	            entropies (`torch.Tensor`):
1420	                Tensor of shape (batch_size, seq_len) with per-token entropy values.
1421	            mask (`torch.Tensor`):
1422	                Binary mask of the same shape as `entropies`, where `1` indicates valid tokens and `0` padding.
1423	            threshold (`float`):
1424	                Quantile threshold between `0.0` and `1.0` to select high-entropy tokens.
1425	
1426	        Returns:
1427	            `torch.Tensor`:
1428	                Boolean mask of shape (batch_size, seq_len), where `True` indicates tokens with entropy >= threshold
1429	                and `False` otherwise.
1430	        """
1431	        local = entropies[mask.bool()].float()
1432	
1433	        # Use a negative pad_value as a sentinel because entropy values are always >= 0.
1434	        # This guarantees that the sentinel cannot collide with any real entropy value.
1435	        pad_value = -1e9
1436	
1437	        # Pad across processes so that every rank has the same tensor length
1438	        padded = self.accelerator.pad_across_processes(local, dim=0, pad_index=pad_value)
1439	        gathered = self.accelerator.gather(padded)
1440	
1441	        # Drop sentinel values (safe because no entropy can be negative)
1442	        gathered = gathered[gathered != pad_value]
1443	
1444	        if gathered.numel() == 0:
1445	            return torch.zeros_like(entropies, dtype=torch.bool)
1446	
1447	        entropy_threshold = torch.quantile(gathered, threshold)
1448	        masked_entropies = entropies * mask.float()
1449	        entropy_mask = masked_entropies >= entropy_threshold
1450	        return entropy_mask & mask.bool()  # ensure padding tokens are always masked out

1453	    def _get_per_token_logps_and_entropies(
1454	        self,
1455	        model,
1456	        input_ids,
1457	        attention_mask,
1458	        logits_to_keep,
1459	        batch_size=None,
1460	        compute_entropy=False,

1473	        """Compute log-probs, (optionally) entropies, and (optionally) the MoE load-balancing aux loss."""
1474	        batch_size = batch_size or input_ids.size(0)  # Chunk inputs into smaller batches to reduce memory peak
1475	        all_logps = []
1476	        all_entropies = []
1477	        all_aux_losses = []
1478	        for start in range(0, input_ids.size(0), batch_size):
1479	            end = min(start + batch_size, input_ids.size(0))  # the last chunk can be smaller than batch_size
1480	            input_ids_batch = input_ids[start:end]
1481	            attention_mask_batch = attention_mask[start:end]
1482	
1483	            # Build model inputs
1484	            model_inputs = {"input_ids": input_ids_batch, "attention_mask": attention_mask_batch}
1485	            if num_images is not None:
1486	                cum_imgs = torch.tensor([0] + num_images).cumsum(0)
1487	                img_start, img_end = cum_imgs[start], cum_imgs[end]
1488	            if image_grid_thw is not None and pixel_values is not None:
1489	                rows_per_image = image_grid_thw.prod(dim=-1)
1490	                rows_per_sample = torch.split(rows_per_image, num_images)
1491	                rows_per_sample = torch.stack([s.sum() for s in rows_per_sample])
1492	                cum_rows = torch.cat([torch.tensor([0], device=rows_per_sample.device), rows_per_sample.cumsum(0)])
1493	                row_start, row_end = cum_rows[start].item(), cum_rows[end].item()
1494	                model_inputs["pixel_values"] = pixel_values[row_start:row_end]
1495	                model_inputs["image_grid_thw"] = image_grid_thw[img_start:img_end]
1496	            elif image_position_ids is not None and pixel_values is not None:
1497	                model_inputs["pixel_values"] = pixel_values[img_start:img_end]
1498	                model_inputs["image_position_ids"] = image_position_ids[img_start:img_end]
1499	            elif spatial_shapes is not None and pixel_values is not None:
1500	                # LFM2-VL tensors are tile-indexed.
1501	                cum_tiles = torch.tensor([0] + num_tiles).cumsum(0)
1502	                tile_start, tile_end = cum_tiles[start], cum_tiles[end]
1503	                model_inputs["pixel_values"] = pixel_values[tile_start:tile_end]

1506	            elif num_tiles is not None and pixel_values is not None:
1507	                # InternVL tensors are tile-indexed.
1508	                cum_tiles = torch.tensor([0] + num_tiles).cumsum(0)
1509	                tile_start, tile_end = cum_tiles[start], cum_tiles[end]
1510	                model_inputs["pixel_values"] = pixel_values[tile_start:tile_end]
1511	            elif pixel_values is not None and pixel_values.size(0) == sum(num_images):

1513	            elif pixel_values is not None:
1514	                model_inputs["pixel_values"] = pixel_values[start:end]
1515	            if pixel_attention_mask is not None and spatial_shapes is None:
1516	                model_inputs["pixel_attention_mask"] = pixel_attention_mask[start:end]
1517	            if image_sizes is not None:
1518	                model_inputs["image_sizes"] = image_sizes[img_start:img_end]
1519	            if token_type_ids is not None:
1520	                model_inputs["token_type_ids"] = token_type_ids[start:end]
1521	            if mm_token_type_ids is not None:
1522	                model_inputs["mm_token_type_ids"] = mm_token_type_ids[start:end]
1523	
1524	            # Only add logits_to_keep if the model supports it
1525	            if "logits_to_keep" in self.model_kwarg_keys:
1526	                # We add 1 to `logits_to_keep` because the last logits of the sequence is later excluded
1527	                model_inputs["logits_to_keep"] = logits_to_keep + 1
1528	
1529	            model_inputs["use_cache"] = False  # only used in generation; set False to suppress warnings

1532	            # as a forward kwarg (not from the model config), so it must be passed here.
1533	            if compute_aux_loss:

1536	            outputs = model(**model_inputs)
1537	            logits = outputs.logits
1538	            # Exclude the last value: it corresponds to the next token pred
1539	            logits = logits[:, :-1, :]  # (B, L-1, H)
1540	            # Only keep the last logits_to_keep. For model that support logits_to_keep, this is a no-op.
1541	            logits = logits[:, -logits_to_keep:, :]  # (B, logits_to_keep, H)

1563	        logps = torch.cat(all_logps, dim=0)

1579	    @profiling_decorator
1580	    def _prepare_inputs(self, generation_batch: dict[str, torch.Tensor | Any]) -> dict[str, torch.Tensor | Any]:
1581	        # Prepares inputs for model training/evaluation by managing completion generation and batch handling.
1582	        # During training:
1583	        #   - Receives the local generation batch (Per-GPU batch size × steps per generation)
1584	        #     from the modified training dataloader instead of the standard local batch
1585	        #   - Generates completions once for the entire generation batch and splits it into batches of size
1586	        #     `per_device_train_batch_size`
1587	        #   - Buffers these completions and returns the appropriate slice for the current accumulation step
1588	        #   - Optimizes by regenerating completions only periodically (every steps_per_generation * num_iterations)
1589	        # During evaluation:
1590	        #   - The input is treated as a standard local batch (no accumulation, no multiple iterations)
1591	        #   - Completions are generated for each batch without buffering or reuse
1592	        # Returns a single local batch in both cases.
1593	
1594	        mode = "train" if self.model.training else "eval"
1595	        if mode == "train":
1596	            generate_every = self.args.steps_per_generation * self.num_iterations
1597	            if self._step % generate_every == 0 or self._buffered_inputs is None:
1598	                # self._buffered_inputs=None can occur when resuming from a checkpoint
1599	                generation_batch = self._generate_and_score_completions(generation_batch)
1600	                generation_batch = split_pixel_values_by_grid(generation_batch)
1601	                generation_batch = shuffle_sequence_dict(generation_batch)
1602	                generation_batches = split_tensor_dict(generation_batch, self.args.steps_per_generation)
1603	                self._buffered_inputs = [unsplit_pixel_values_by_grid(batch) for batch in generation_batches]
1604	            inputs = self._buffered_inputs[self._step % self.args.steps_per_generation]
1605	        else:
1606	            # In evaluation, there is neither batch grouping for generation, nor multiple iterations, hence
1607	            # local generation batch == local eval batch
1608	            inputs = self._generate_and_score_completions(generation_batch)
1609	        return inputs

896	    # Compute variance ignoring NaNs
897	    mean = torch.nanmean(tensor, dim=dim, keepdim=True)
898	    variance = torch.nanmean((tensor - mean) ** 2, dim=dim, keepdim=True)
899	    count = torch.sum(~torch.isnan(tensor), dim=dim, keepdim=True)  # count of non-NaN values
900	    correction = count / (count - 1)
901	    correction = torch.where(count > 1, correction, torch.full_like(correction, float("nan")))

911	    for d in sorted(dims, reverse=True):

55	    seq_log_ratio = torch.sum(log_ratio_clamped * mask, dim=-1, keepdim=True)  # (B, 1)

3039	    def get_off_policy_mask(
3040	        advantages: torch.Tensor,
3041	        per_token_logps: torch.Tensor,
3042	        sampling_per_token_logps: torch.Tensor,
3043	        mask: torch.Tensor,
3044	        off_policy_threshold: float,
3045	    ) -> torch.Tensor:
3046	        """
3047	        Computes the Off-Policy Sequence Mask from DeepSeek-V3.2 paper. Returns a (B, 1) tensor where 1.0 indicates
3048	        "Keep" and 0.0 indicates "Drop".
3049	        """
3050	        # forward KL div: log(pi_old) - log(pi_theta)
3051	        kl_div = sampling_per_token_logps - per_token_logps.detach()
3052	        # Tokens vLLM could not score carry NaN and provide no KL evidence. Left in, the sequence mean is NaN,
3053	        # `avg_seq_kl <= off_policy_threshold` is then False, and a negative-advantage sequence would be dropped
3054	        # on the strength of a single unscorable token.
3055	        kl_div = torch.nan_to_num(kl_div, nan=0.0)
3056	        # Sequence-level Mean KL (ignoring prompt+padding)
3057	        seq_kl_sum = (kl_div * mask).sum(dim=1, keepdim=True)
3058	        avg_seq_kl = seq_kl_sum / mask.sum(dim=1, keepdim=True).clamp(min=1.0)
3059	        # Keep if (Advantage >= 0) OR (KL <= delta)
3060	        is_pos_adv = advantages >= 0
3061	        is_low_kl = avg_seq_kl <= off_policy_threshold

3064	    @staticmethod
3065	    @torch.no_grad()
3066	    def get_gamma_weights(
3067	        advantages: torch.Tensor,
3068	        log_ratio_per_token: torch.Tensor,
3069	        mask: torch.Tensor,
3070	        importance_sampling_ratio: torch.Tensor | None,  # (B, T)
3071	        k_pos: float = 2.0,
3072	        lambda_pos: float = 3.0,
3073	        k_neg: float = 3.0,
3074	        lambda_neg: float = 2.0,
3075	    ) -> torch.Tensor:
3076	        """
3077	        Computes the Gamma weights for the VESPO loss. For reference:
3078	            φ(w) = e^λ × w^k × e^{-λw} is the gamma weighting (normalized so φ(1)=1)
3079	                with w = sequence-level importance sampling ratio
3080	        note: we will compute φ(w) in log space
3081	
3082	        φ(w) is detached via @torch.no_grad(), only acts as gradient scaling coefficient
3083	
3084	        VESPO loss = -φ(w) × A × log_prob, gradient naturally gives φ(w) × A × ∇log π
3085	        """
3086	        # reducing clamp range directly to log(1e-8) ~ -18.42, to avoid recomputing log_w=log(w.clamp(min=1e-8)) later
3087	        # This is solely for matching truthfully the original implementation, otherwise keeping -20 could be fine.
3088	        lower_clamp = math.log(1e-8)
3089	
3090	        # Sequence-level log ratio Σ log(π_θ/π_old) (not a mean like for `log_importance_weights`)
3091	        log_ratio_clamped = torch.clamp(log_ratio_per_token, -20.0, 20.0)
3092	        seq_log_ratio = torch.sum(log_ratio_clamped * mask, dim=-1, keepdim=True)  # (B, 1)
3093	
3094	        # Apply token-level TIS or MIS correction (in log space)
3095	        if importance_sampling_ratio is not None:
3096	            log_is_ratio = torch.clamp(torch.log(importance_sampling_ratio), lower_clamp, 20.0)
3097	            # log(w) = log(π_θ/π_old) + log(π_old/π_sampler)
3098	            seq_log_ratio += torch.sum(log_is_ratio, dim=-1, keepdim=True)
3099	
3100	        log_w_seq = torch.clamp(seq_log_ratio, lower_clamp, 20.0)
3101	        w_seq = torch.exp(log_w_seq)
3102	
3103	        # compute k and lambda based on advantage sign
3104	        is_nonneg_adv = advantages >= 0
3105	        k_seq = torch.where(is_nonneg_adv, k_pos, k_neg)
3106	        lambda_seq = torch.where(is_nonneg_adv, lambda_pos, lambda_neg).clamp(min=1e-4)
3107	
3108	        # log(φ(w)) = λ + k × log(w) - λ × w
3109	        log_phi = lambda_seq + k_seq * log_w_seq - lambda_seq * w_seq
3110	        phi_seq = torch.exp(log_phi).nan_to_num(nan=0.0, posinf=0.0, neginf=0.0)
3111	
3112	        return phi_seq  # (B, 1)

3388	    def prediction_step(self, model, inputs, prediction_loss_only, ignore_keys: list[str] | None = None):
3389	        inputs = self._prepare_inputs(inputs)

3396	    def log(self, logs: dict[str, float], start_time: float | None = None) -> None:
3397	        mode = "train" if self.model.training else "eval"
3398	        # Average the metrics
3399	        metrics = {}
3400	        for key, val in self._metrics[mode].items():
3401	            # Filter out NaN values before averaging. A reward function that returns None for all samples
3402	            # in a batch produces NaN for that batch's metric. With logging_steps > 1, a naive sum()/len()
3403	            # would let a single NaN contaminate valid data from other batches. Only return None when no
3404	            # valid values remain (e.g. JSON loggers crash on float NaN).
3405	            valid = [v for v in val if not math.isnan(v)]
3406	            metrics[key] = sum(valid) / len(valid) if valid else None
3407	
3408	        # This method can be called both in training and evaluation. When called in evaluation, the keys in `logs`
3409	        # start with "eval_". We need to add the prefix "eval_" to the keys in `metrics` to match the format.
3410	        if mode == "eval":

200	        vespo_k_neg (`float`, *optional*, defaults to `3.0`):

202	            we down-weight samples with low importance weights (when the importance sampling ratio < 1).
203	        vespo_lambda_neg (`float`, *optional*, defaults to `2.0`):
204	            lambda parameter for negative advantages, it is the exponential decay factor in the VESPO loss. Controls
205	            how aggressively we down-weight samples with high importance weights (when the importance sampling ratio >

208	            Controls whether importance sampling ratios are computed at the `"token"` or `"sequence"` level. `"token"`
209	            keeps the raw per-token log-probability ratios (one weight per token). `"sequence"` averages the
210	            log-probability ratios across valid tokens to produce a single ratio per sequence. The [GSPO
211	            paper](https://huggingface.co/papers/2507.18071) shows that sequence-level sampling often yields more

214	            Weights for each reward function. Must match the number of reward functions. If `None`, all rewards are
215	            weighted equally with weight `1.0`.
216	        multi_objective_aggregation (`str`, *optional*, defaults to `"sum_then_normalize"`):
217	            Method to aggregate multiple reward functions. Supported values are:
218	
219	            - `"sum_then_normalize"` (default): First sums the weighted rewards from each reward function, then applies
220	              reward scaling/normalization as specified by `scale_rewards` (see `scale_rewards` for details).
221	            - `"normalize_then_sum"`: First normalizes/scales each reward function across generations (within each
222	              group), then sums the normalized rewards using the specified weights. The aggregated reward is then
223	              normalized at the batch level when forming advantages. This is the suggested approach from the paper
224	              [GDPO: Group reward-Decoupled Normalization Policy Optimization for Multi-reward RL

228

237	            Specifies the loss formulation to use. Supported values are:
238

240	              length bias—this approach tends to prefer shorter completions with positive advantages and longer ones
241	              with negative advantages.

243	              introduced in the [Dr. GRPO paper](https://huggingface.co/papers/2503.20783) to eliminate length bias.
244	              The value of the constant corresponds to `max_completion_length`.
245	            - `"dapo"` (default): Aggregates token-level losses by normalizing with the number of active token in the
246	              global accumulated batch. This method was introduced in the [DAPO
247	              paper](https://huggingface.co/papers/2503.14476) to eliminate length bias.
248	            - `"bnpo"`: Aggregates token-level losses by normalizing with the number of active token in the local

259	              learning signals.

261	              sequence's loss by its length. This is a modification of GSPO and requires
262	              `importance_sampling_level="sequence"`. Introduced in the [LUSPO
263	              paper](https://huggingface.co/papers/2602.05261).
264	            - `"vespo"`: Variational Sequence-Level Soft Policy Optimization. Replaces hard clipping with a smooth,
265	              asymmetric Gamma weighting function applied directly to sequence-level importance weights. Introduced in
266	              the [VESPO paper](https://huggingface.co/papers/2602.10693).

277	            between the current policy and the previous reference policy during updates. The reference policy is

2979	            inputs.get("image_grid_thw"),

2989	        lm_head_bias = unwrapped_model.lm_head.bias
2990	        # Liger reads `lm_head` directly instead of through `model.forward()`, so its ZeRO-3 gather hook never fires and
2991	        # the fused matmul gets an empty shard. Gather the weight/bias ourselves for the call (the weight grad is
2992	        # computed during this forward, so it isn't needed in the backward).
2993	        with maybe_gather_lm_head_ctx(lm_head_weight, lm_head_bias):

2995	                _input=last_hidden_state,

2997	                selected_token_ids=completion_ids,

3038	    @staticmethod
3039	    def get_off_policy_mask(
3040	        advantages: torch.Tensor,
3041	        per_token_logps: torch.Tensor,
3042	        sampling_per_token_logps: torch.Tensor,
3043	        mask: torch.Tensor,
3044	        off_policy_threshold: float,
3045	    ) -> torch.Tensor:
3046	        """
3047	        Computes the Off-Policy Sequence Mask from DeepSeek-V3.2 paper. Returns a (B, 1) tensor where 1.0 indicates
3048	        "Keep" and 0.0 indicates "Drop".
3049	        """
3050	        # forward KL div: log(pi_old) - log(pi_theta)
3051	        kl_div = sampling_per_token_logps - per_token_logps.detach()
3052	        # Tokens vLLM could not score carry NaN and provide no KL evidence. Left in, the sequence mean is NaN,
3053	        # `avg_seq_kl <= off_policy_threshold` is then False, and a negative-advantage sequence would be dropped
3054	        # on the strength of a single unscorable token.
3055	        kl_div = torch.nan_to_num(kl_div, nan=0.0)
3056	        # Sequence-level Mean KL (ignoring prompt+padding)
3057	        seq_kl_sum = (kl_div * mask).sum(dim=1, keepdim=True)
3058	        avg_seq_kl = seq_kl_sum / mask.sum(dim=1, keepdim=True).clamp(min=1.0)
3059	        # Keep if (Advantage >= 0) OR (KL <= delta)
3060	        is_pos_adv = advantages >= 0
3061	        is_low_kl = avg_seq_kl <= off_policy_threshold
3062	        return (is_pos_adv | is_low_kl).to(dtype=mask.dtype)  # (B, 1)

3064	    @staticmethod
3065	    @torch.no_grad()
3066	    def get_gamma_weights(
3067	        advantages: torch.Tensor,
3068	        log_ratio_per_token: torch.Tensor,
3069	        mask: torch.Tensor,
3070	        importance_sampling_ratio: torch.Tensor | None,  # (B, T)
3071	        k_pos: float = 2.0,
3072	        lambda_pos: float = 3.0,
3073	        k_neg: float = 3.0,
3074	        lambda_neg: float = 2.0,
3075	    ) -> torch.Tensor:
3076	        """
3077	        Computes the Gamma weights for the VESPO loss. For reference:
3078	            φ(w) = e^λ × w^k × e^{-λw} is the gamma weighting (normalized so φ(1)=1)
3079	                with w = sequence-level importance sampling ratio
3080	        note: we will compute φ(w) in log space
3081	
3082	        φ(w) is detached via @torch.no_grad(), only acts as gradient scaling coefficient
3083	
3084	        VESPO loss = -φ(w) × A × log_prob, gradient naturally gives φ(w) × A × ∇log π
3085	        """
3086	        # reducing clamp range directly to log(1e-8) ~ -18.42, to avoid recomputing log_w=log(w.clamp(min=1e-8)) later
3087	        # This is solely for matching truthfully the original implementation, otherwise keeping -20 could be fine.
3088	        lower_clamp = math.log(1e-8)
3089	
3090	        # Sequence-level log ratio Σ log(π_θ/π_old) (not a mean like for `log_importance_weights`)
3091	        log_ratio_clamped = torch.clamp(log_ratio_per_token, -20.0, 20.0)
3092	        seq_log_ratio = torch.sum(log_ratio_clamped * mask, dim=-1, keepdim=True)  # (B, 1)
3093	
3094	        # Apply token-level TIS or MIS correction (in log space)
3095	        if importance_sampling_ratio is not None:
3096	            log_is_ratio = torch.clamp(torch.log(importance_sampling_ratio), lower_clamp, 20.0)
3097	            # log(w) = log(π_θ/π_old) + log(π_old/π_sampler)
3098	            seq_log_ratio += torch.sum(log_is_ratio, dim=-1, keepdim=True)
3099	
3100	        log_w_seq = torch.clamp(seq_log_ratio, lower_clamp, 20.0)
3101	        w_seq = torch.exp(log_w_seq)
3102	
3103	        # compute k and lambda based on advantage sign
3104	        is_nonneg_adv = advantages >= 0
3105	        k_seq = torch.where(is_nonneg_adv, k_pos, k_neg)
3106	        lambda_seq = torch.where(is_nonneg_adv, lambda_pos, lambda_neg).clamp(min=1e-4)
3107	
3108	        # log(φ(w)) = λ + k × log(w) - λ × w
3109	        log_phi = lambda_seq + k_seq * log_w_seq - lambda_seq * w_seq
3110	        phi_seq = torch.exp(log_phi).nan_to_num(nan=0.0, posinf=0.0, neginf=0.0)
3111	
3112	        return phi_seq  # (B, 1)

19	def resolve_accelerate_config_argument(launch_args: list[str]) -> list[str]:
20	    """
21	    Resolve `--accelerate_config` from CLI arguments into `accelerate --config_file`.
22	
23	    The function supports either a filesystem path or a predefined config name shipped in `trl/accelerate_configs`
24	    (without the `.yaml` suffix).
25	    """
26	    if "--accelerate_config" not in launch_args:
27	        return launch_args
28	
29	    config_index = launch_args.index("--accelerate_config")
30	    if config_index + 1 >= len(launch_args):
31	        raise ValueError("Expected a value after `--accelerate_config`.")
32	
33	    config_name = launch_args[config_index + 1]
34	    if Path(config_name).is_file():
35	        accelerate_config_path = config_name
36	    else:
37	        candidate = resources.files("trl.accelerate_configs").joinpath(f"{config_name}.yaml")
38	        if not candidate.exists():
39	            raise ValueError(
40	                f"Accelerate config {config_name} is neither a file nor a valid config in the `trl` package. "
41	                "Please provide a valid config name or a path to a config file."
42	            )
43	        accelerate_config_path = candidate
44	
45	    # Remove '--accelerate_config <value>'.
46	    launch_args = launch_args[:config_index] + launch_args[config_index + 2 :]
47	    return ["--config_file", str(accelerate_config_path)] + launch_args

68	def main(script_args, training_args, model_args, dataset_args):
69	    from accelerate.logging import get_logger
70	    from datasets import load_dataset
71	
72	    from trl import GRPOTrainer, get_dataset, get_peft_config, get_quantization_config
73	    from trl.rewards import (
74	        accuracy_reward,
75	        get_soft_overlong_punishment,
76	        reasoning_accuracy_reward,
77	        think_format_reward,
78	    )
79	
80	    logger = get_logger(__name__)
81	
82	    reward_funcs_registry = {
83	        "accuracy_reward": accuracy_reward,
84	        "reasoning_accuracy_reward": reasoning_accuracy_reward,
85	        "think_format_reward": think_format_reward,
86	        "get_soft_overlong_punishment": get_soft_overlong_punishment(max_completion_len=1280, soft_punish_cache=256),
87	    }
88	
89	    # Get the reward models and functions
90	    reward_funcs = []
91	    if script_args.reward_model_name_or_path:
92	        reward_funcs.append(script_args.reward_model_name_or_path)
93	
94	    if script_args.reward_funcs:
95	        for func_name in script_args.reward_funcs:
96	            if func_name in reward_funcs_registry:
97	                reward_funcs.append(reward_funcs_registry[func_name])
98	            elif "." in func_name:
99	                module_path, func_name = func_name.rsplit(".", 1)
100	                sys.path.insert(0, os.getcwd())
101	                module = importlib.import_module(module_path)
102	                reward_func = getattr(module, func_name)
103	                reward_funcs.append(reward_func)
104	            else:
105	                raise ValueError(
106	                    f"Could not load reward function '{func_name}'. Expected one of "
107	                    f"{list(reward_funcs_registry.keys())} or a valid import path."
108	                )
109	
110	    training_args.model_init_kwargs = dict(
111	        revision=model_args.model_revision,
112	        trust_remote_code=training_args.trust_remote_code,
113	        attn_implementation=model_args.attn_implementation,
114	        dtype=model_args.dtype,
115	    )
116	
117	    # Load the dataset
118	    if dataset_args.datasets and script_args.dataset_name:
119	        logger.warning(
120	            "Both `datasets` and `dataset_name` are provided. The `datasets` argument will be used to load the "
121	            "dataset and `dataset_name` will be ignored."
122	        )
123	        dataset = get_dataset(dataset_args)
124	    elif dataset_args.datasets and not script_args.dataset_name:
125	        dataset = get_dataset(dataset_args)
126	    elif not dataset_args.datasets and script_args.dataset_name:
127	        dataset = load_dataset(
128	            script_args.dataset_name, name=script_args.dataset_config, streaming=script_args.dataset_streaming
129	        )
130	    else:
131	        raise ValueError("Either `datasets` or `dataset_name` must be provided.")
132	
133	    # Initialize the GRPO trainer
134	    trainer = GRPOTrainer(
135	        model=model_args.model_name_or_path,
136	        reward_funcs=reward_funcs,
137	        args=training_args,
138	        train_dataset=dataset[script_args.dataset_train_split],
139	        eval_dataset=dataset[script_args.dataset_test_split] if training_args.eval_strategy != "no" else None,
140	        quantization_config=get_quantization_config(model_args),
141	        peft_config=get_peft_config(model_args),
142	    )
143	
144	    # Train the model
145	    trainer.train()
146	
147	    # Log training complete
148	    trainer.accelerator.print("✅ Training completed.")
149	
150	    # Save and push to Hub
151	    trainer.save_model(training_args.output_dir)
152	    trainer.accelerator.print(f"💾 Model saved to {training_args.output_dir}.")
153	
154	    if training_args.push_to_hub:
155	        trainer.push_to_hub(dataset_name=script_args.dataset_name)
156	        trainer.accelerator.print(f"🤗 Model pushed to the Hub in https://huggingface.co/{trainer.hub_model_id}.")

Should identify concrete bugs likely in run wrappers. Obvious:
- capture_logps set model.training but model argument can DDP? DDP has training yes. During _compute_loss, self.model.training used mode. Records result[0] detached correct concatenated chunks. Could stale recorded_logps if Liger? use_liger false config so no issue. But generic wrapper if use_liger true _compute_loss not called (compute_loss Liger) so no records, not necessarily user configured.
- filename state.global_step and record_index. record_index not resumed from checkpoint, on resume new files start batch00000 and step current resumes global step e.g6 so unique due step. record_index global local count. Within same step multiple num_iterations etc unique. On resumed from checkpoint at same global step? Trainer resumes after step, no same filenames unless checkpoint at end then no more. If existing partial output retry same step maybe overwrite okay.
- resume _step not restored by GRPO itself? Known base issue? _step set 0 and _buffered_inputs None; resume mid generation generation scheduling different but not wrapper? Should inspect training train resume semantics. On resume self._step 0 and skip batches based global steps, _prepare_inputs generate_every and buffer. Could cause generation schedule / step index mismatches and record_index. Should derive.
- RecordMetrics on_log writes every process to own rank file good; directory made output earlier. json serialization may fail numpy values etc logs Python floats mostly. Known rank0 custom gather crash excluded.
- on_log logs may be None causing TypeError but callback contract logs dict. kwargs not forwarded irrelevant callback.
- capture_logps with exceptions leaves flag true and subsequent eval? If super raises training abort.
- model.training false for eval means no capture. Fine.
- `loss=float(loss.detach())` triggers GPU sync, okay, stored scaled optimization loss. It is per microbatch scaled DAPO as intended. `generation_token_count=float(inputs["num_items_in_batch"])` 0-d tensor CUDA conversion works.
- `previous = logps if previous is None else previous`, logps detached. Correct matching _compute_loss old fallback.
- output records mask uses completion_mask only but actual loss mask includes tool_mask; config no tools. In generic bug if tools.
- output records logps capture result[0] from any invocation while flag true. _compute_loss only calls once. Chunked method concatenates full logps then returns, wrapper captures after super returns. Good.
- DDP model.training: when evaluate model.eval, RecordedGRPO._compute_loss not called? prediction_step compute_loss calls _compute_loss, capture false. Good.
- `model.training` may be true even when trainer eval? Base evaluation sets model.eval then restore. correct.
- DDP no issues attributes only self.
- gradient checkpointing: overridden `_get_per_token...` decorated profiling perhaps super calls multiple forwards? Captures result. If gradient checkpointing non-reentrant, during backward model forward recomputed? At time capture false set before backward, no capture overwritten. Good. reentrant checkpointing forward replay occurs during backward? wrapper capture false so no writes.
- `recorded_logps` initialized only upon first captured call. no issue.
- gradient accumulation `current_gradient_accumulation_steps` dynamic; recorded per loss. Fine.
- `record_index` not checkpointed: resume output sequence restarts batch numbering. Filenames include global step so no overwrite if standard. But output records on resumed training may have same step? If checkpoint saved at step6 and training crash during step7 before next checkpoint, resume step6, existing token record step6? At checkpoint step6 records batches indices 10,11 etc, after resume state6 next is global step7 eventually filenames step6 during microbatches because state.global_step increments after optimizer. Existing step6 from prior completed step6. Retry same step7 was state6 records may have been written before crash; after resume records again same `step0006_batch00012...`? record_index resets 0, so not same, leaves stale duplicates with differing indices. Optimization records inaccurate duplicates. Could candidate.

Should inspect dependencies versions exact Trainer source, training step model wrapping and eval. Can read installed package via python? No network/training allowed. Python introspection read-only okay but environment cautions Python -I. Better locate using `python -I -c import inspect...` but importing workspace? -I removes cwd but env PYTHONPATH? isolated ignores. Could find /usr/local/lib/python... Use bash find. Also repo tests may reveal intended behavior and known bugs. Search RecordedGRPO references results maybe output artifacts actual. Should inspect results existing to understand observed. User asks maximum recall review likely find 8 issues in code. I should systematically audit.

`_get_per_token_logps_and_entropies(self,*args,**kwargs)` forwards perfectly. Base compute_loss call doesn't pass batch_size, default full microbatch. During generation old/ref logps calls `_get_per_token...` while capture_logps false. During training capture true only set just before super. correct.
But `_compute_loss` is called via Liger? no. Fine.
Metrics callback on_log may record training and evaluation under same `step` global; metrics_rank includes final evaluate logs `eval_loss` etc at same final step and training logs. Valid but final_metrics rank0 only.

Main setup:
- `args.output.mkdir` on all ranks concurrent exist_ok true fine.
- Dataset map in each process perhaps file locking cache; okay.
- rollout path opened append per rank, on resume appends no truncation, duplicates possible expected resume? output records resumption duplication issue.
- record_directory token_records mkdir(exist_ok=True) no parents but args.output exists. concurrent ranks mkdir exist_ok true safe.
- np.savez writes directly to final path, no atomicity. DDP distinct rank filenames. If crash midwrite leaves corrupt file, resume writes different filename due record_index reset so corrupt remains. Candidate but maybe lower severity.
- `float(loss.detach())` CPU sync valid.
- state.global_step during record is previous completed optimizer steps, all microbatches of next update labeled previous step. Should understand. steps_per_generation4 and grad_accum2 means generation batch spans 2 optimization steps. This is intended. num_items spans generation batch gathered all ranks. DAPO normalizer current accumulation/steps generation factor. Good.

Potential major recording issue: self.recorded_logps stores only current policy forward. Base `_compute_loss` computes `policy_loss = loss.detach()` after scaling, records loss. good. But with DDP and grad accumulation no sync on second? actual loss records each local microbatch, world size. okay.

Potential base bug around `mode = self.model.training` vs `model.training` under DDP? User focus handles DDP/model.training/eval maybe wrapper uses model.training which can disagree with self.model.training? Usually same. Under compile wrappers maybe model.training true. DDP inherits Module training and `.eval()` recurses. Fine.

But capturing based `model.training` rather than `self.model.training` likely correct for actual model passed. If model is custom wrapper whose training flag not synchronized? accelerate wrapper always.

Potential problem with capture_logps boolean shared across calls: reference/old logps generated inside `_compute_loss`? Base _compute_loss doesn't call others except current. no.

Potential gradient accumulation microbatch chunking: base `_get_per_token_logps_and_entropies` default `batch_size = batch_size or input_ids.size(0)` so no internal chunks unless passed. During training base call no batch_size => full. During generation calls with batch_size config maybe per_device. Wrapper capture false. If future base passes chunk size, concatenated correct. No bug.

Potential kwargs forwarding: `_get_per_token...(*args,**kwargs)` fine. `_compute_loss(self, model, inputs)` base exact. `_save_checkpoint` only base. RecordMetrics `on_log` accepts kwargs. Fine.

Should inspect GRPO other calls to `_get_per_token` in generate block to ensure captured "right forward" when capture flag might still true from prior call due timing. Read 2558-2940.

1253	    def _get_train_sampler(self, dataset: Dataset | None = None) -> Sampler:
1254	        # Returns a sampler that
1255	        # 1. ensures each prompt is repeated across multiple processes. This guarantees that identical prompts are
1256	        #    distributed to different GPUs, allowing rewards to be computed and normalized correctly within each prompt
1257	        #    group. Using the same seed across processes ensures consistent prompt assignment, preventing discrepancies
1258	        #    in group formation.
1259	        # 2. repeats the batch multiple times to allow reusing generations across multiple updates. Refer to
1260	        #    _prepare_inputs to see how the generations are stored and reused.
1261	
1262	        # In the following figure, the values are the prompt indices. Each row shows the per-step batch
1263	        # returned by `_prepare_inputs`; rows within a `steps_per_generation` block are slices of the same
1264	        # generated batch. When `num_iterations > 1`, that block is reused for multiple optimization passes
1265	        # before regenerating.
1266	        #
1267	        #                                      |   GPU 0  |   GPU 1  |
1268	        #
1269	        #                 global_step   step    <-───>  num_generations=2
1270	        #                                       <-───────> per_device_train_batch_size=3
1271	        #  grad_accum    ▲  ▲  0          0     0   0   1   1   2   2   <- Generate for the first `steps_per_generation` (prompts 0 to 11); store the completions; use the first slice to compute the loss
1272	        #     =2         ▼  |  0          1     3   3   4   4   5   5   <- Take the stored generations and use the second slice to compute the loss
1273	        #                   |
1274	        #                   |  1          2     6   6   7   7   8   8   <- Take the stored generations and use the third slice to compute the loss
1275	        #  steps_per_gen=4  ▼  1          3     9   9  10  10  11  11   <- Take the stored generations and use the fourth slice to compute the loss
1276	        #
1277	        #                      2          4    12  12  13  13  14  14   <- Generate for the second `steps_per_generation` (prompts 12 to 23); store the completions; use the first slice to compute the loss
1278	        #                      2          5    15  15  16  16  17  17   <- Take the stored generations and use the second slice to compute the loss
1279	        #                                          ...
1280	        if dataset is None:
1281	            dataset = self.train_dataset
1282	        return RepeatSampler(
1283	            data_source=dataset,
1284	            mini_repeat_count=self.num_generations,
1285	            batch_size=self.args.generation_batch_size // self.num_generations,
1286	            repeat_count=self.num_iterations * self.args.steps_per_generation,
1287	            shuffle=self.shuffle_dataset,
1288	            seed=self.args.seed,
1289	        )

881	    """

883	
884	    Args:

886	            Input tensor.

898	    variance = torch.nanmean((tensor - mean) ** 2, dim=dim, keepdim=True)
899	    count = torch.sum(~torch.isnan(tensor), dim=dim, keepdim=True)  # count of non-NaN values
900	    correction = count / (count - 1)
901	    correction = torch.where(count > 1, correction, torch.full_like(correction, float("nan")))

910	    dims = [(d if d >= 0 else d + std.ndim) for d in dim]
911	    for d in sorted(dims, reverse=True):
912	        std = std.squeeze(d)

17	from contextlib import contextmanager
18

20	class DistributedBackend:
21	    """Abstracts distributed backend specifics (DeepSpeed ZeRO, FSDP) behind a uniform API.
22	
23	    Detects the active backend once at construction from ``accelerator.state``, then provides context managers that are
24	    no-ops on backends where the operation is not needed.
25	
26	    Args:
27	        accelerator ([`~accelerate.Accelerator`]):
28	            The accelerator instance managing the distributed state.
29	
30	    Example:
31	
32	    ```python
33	    >>> dist = DistributedBackend(accelerator)
34	    >>> with dist.gather_params(list(model.parameters())):
35	    ...     model.merge_adapter()
36	    >>> with dist.summon_full_params(model, recurse=False):
37	    ...     outputs = model.generate(inputs)
38	    ```
39	    """
40	
41	    def __init__(self, accelerator):
42	        ds_plugin = accelerator.state.deepspeed_plugin
43	        fsdp_plugin = getattr(accelerator.state, "fsdp_plugin", None)
44	        self.zero_stage = ds_plugin.zero_stage if ds_plugin else 0
45	        self.fsdp_version = getattr(fsdp_plugin, "fsdp_version", None) if fsdp_plugin else None
46	
47	    @property
48	    def is_zero3(self) -> bool:
49	        """Whether DeepSpeed ZeRO Stage 3 is active."""
50	        return self.zero_stage == 3
51	
52	    @property
53	    def is_fsdp(self) -> bool:
54	        """Whether FSDP (any version) is active."""
55	        return self.fsdp_version is not None
56	
57	    @contextmanager
58	    def gather_params(self, params):
59	        """Gather sharded parameters under DeepSpeed ZeRO-3; no-op otherwise.
60	
61	        Args:
62	            params (iterable of `torch.nn.Parameter`):
63	                Parameters to gather.
64	        """
65	        if self.is_zero3:
66	            import deepspeed
67	
68	            with deepspeed.zero.GatheredParameters(params):
69	                yield
70	        else:
71	            yield

74	    def summon_full_params(self, module, **kwargs):
75	        """Materialize full FSDP v1 parameters; no-op for FSDP v2 or non-FSDP backends.

718	class RepeatSampler(Sampler):
719	    """
720	    Sampler that repeats the indices of a dataset in a structured manner.
721	
722	    Args:
723	        data_source (`Sized`):
724	            Dataset to sample from.
725	        mini_repeat_count (`int`):
726	            Number of times to repeat each index per batch.
727	        batch_size (`int`, *optional*, defaults to `1`):
728	            Number of unique indices per batch.
729	        repeat_count (`int`, *optional*, defaults to `1`):
730	            Number of times to repeat the full sampling process.
731	        shuffle (`bool`, *optional*, defaults to `True`):
732	            Whether to shuffle the dataset.
733	        seed (`int`, *optional*):
734	            Random seed for reproducibility (only affects this sampler).
735	
736	    Example:
737	    ```python
738	    >>> sampler = RepeatSampler(["a", "b", "c", "d", "e", "f", "g"], mini_repeat_count=2, batch_size=3, repeat_count=4)
739	    >>> list(sampler)
740	    [4, 4, 3, 3, 0, 0,
741	     4, 4, 3, 3, 0, 0,
742	     4, 4, 3, 3, 0, 0,
743	     4, 4, 3, 3, 0, 0,
744	     1, 1, 2, 2, 6, 6,
745	     1, 1, 2, 2, 6, 6,
746	     1, 1, 2, 2, 6, 6,
747	     1, 1, 2, 2, 6, 6]
748	    ```
749	
750	    ```txt
751	    mini_repeat_count = 3
752	          -   -   -
753	         [0,  0,  0,  1,  1,  1,  2,  2,  2,  3,  3,  3,      |
754	          4,  4,  4,  5,  5,  5,  6,  6,  6,  7,  7,  7,      |
755	          8,  8,  8,  9,  9,  9, 10, 10, 10, 11, 11, 11,      |
756	                                                                repeat_count = 2
757	          0,  0,  0,  1,  1,  1,  2,  2,  2,  3,  3,  3,      |
758	          4,  4,  4,  5,  5,  5,  6,  6,  6,  7,  7,  7,      |
759	          8,  8,  8,  9,  9,  9, 10, 10, 10, 11, 11, 11, ...] |
760	          ---------   ---------   ---------   ---------
761	           ---------   ---------   ---------   ---------
762	            ---------   ---------   ---------   ---------
763	                         batch_size = 12
764	    ```
765	    """
766	
767	    def __init__(
768	        self,
769	        data_source: Sized,
770	        mini_repeat_count: int,
771	        batch_size: int = 1,
772	        repeat_count: int = 1,
773	        shuffle: bool = True,
774	        seed: int | None = None,
775	    ):
776	        self.data_source = data_source
777	        self.mini_repeat_count = mini_repeat_count
778	        self.batch_size = batch_size
779	        self.repeat_count = repeat_count
780	        self.num_samples = len(data_source)
781	        self.shuffle = shuffle
782	        self.seed = seed
783	
784	        if shuffle:
785	            self.generator = torch.Generator()  # Create a local random generator
786	            if seed is not None:
787	                self.generator.manual_seed(seed)
788	
789	    def __iter__(self):
790	        if self.shuffle:
791	            # E.g., [2, 4, 3, 1, 0, 6, 5] (num_samples = 7)
792	            indexes = torch.randperm(self.num_samples, generator=self.generator).tolist()
793	        else:
794	            indexes = list(range(self.num_samples))
795	
796	        #    [2, 4, 3, 1, 0, 6, 5]
797	        # -> [[2, 4, 3], [1, 0, 6], [5]]  (batch_size = 3)
798	        indexes = [indexes[i : i + self.batch_size] for i in range(0, len(indexes), self.batch_size)]
799	
800	        #    [[2, 4, 3], [1, 0, 6], [5]]
801	        # -> [[2, 4, 3], [1, 0, 6]]
802	        indexes = [chunk for chunk in indexes if len(chunk) == self.batch_size]
803	
804	        for chunk in indexes:
805	            for _ in range(self.repeat_count):
806	                for index in chunk:
807	                    for _ in range(self.mini_repeat_count):
808	                        yield index
809	
810	    def __len__(self) -> int:
811	        return (self.num_samples // self.batch_size) * self.batch_size * self.mini_repeat_count * self.repeat_count

814	def repeat_iterable_dataset(
815	    dataset: IterableDataset, mini_repeat_count: int, batch_size: int = 1, repeat_count: int = 1
816	):
817	    """
818	    Streaming counterpart of [`RepeatSampler`] for [`~datasets.IterableDataset`].
819	
820	    An [`~datasets.IterableDataset`] cannot be indexed, so a sampler cannot be attached to it. Instead of reordering
821	    indices, this reorders the *stream* itself with [`~datasets.IterableDataset.map`], producing records in exactly the
822	    same order that [`RepeatSampler`] yields indices for a map-style dataset with the same arguments. Because the
823	    transform stays chained to `dataset`, `set_epoch` propagates to an upstream [`~datasets.IterableDataset.shuffle`]
824	    and the order is reshuffled every epoch, as [`RepeatSampler`] does.
825	
826	    Shuffling is intentionally left out: it is handled upstream via [`~datasets.IterableDataset.shuffle`] (buffered
827	    shuffling), the streaming equivalent of the full permutation done by [`RepeatSampler`].
828	
829	    Args:
830	        dataset (`datasets.IterableDataset`):
831	            Dataset to stream from.
832	        mini_repeat_count (`int`):
833	            Number of times to repeat each record per batch.
834	        batch_size (`int`, *optional*, defaults to `1`):
835	            Number of unique records per batch.
836	        repeat_count (`int`, *optional*, defaults to `1`):
837	            Number of times to repeat the full batch.
838	
839	    Returns:
840	        `datasets.IterableDataset`: Dataset yielding the records of `dataset`, repeated and reordered.
841	
842	    Example:
843	    ```python
844	    >>> from datasets import IterableDataset
845	
846	    >>> dataset = IterableDataset.from_generator(lambda: ({"x": i} for i in range(7)))
847	    >>> repeated = repeat_iterable_dataset(dataset, mini_repeat_count=2, batch_size=3, repeat_count=4)
848	    >>> [record["x"] for record in repeated]
849	    [0, 0, 1, 1, 2, 2,
850	     0, 0, 1, 1, 2, 2,
851	     0, 0, 1, 1, 2, 2,
852	     0, 0, 1, 1, 2, 2,
853	     3, 3, 4, 4, 5, 5,
854	     3, 3, 4, 4, 5, 5,
855	     3, 3, 4, 4, 5, 5,
856	     3, 3, 4, 4, 5, 5]
857	    ```
858	    """
859	
860	    def repeat_batch(batch: dict) -> dict:
861	        # `batch` maps each column to a list of `batch_size` values (fewer for the trailing batch, which is dropped to
862	        # match RepeatSampler). Transpose it back to records, repeating them as RepeatSampler repeats indices. Records
863	        # are deep-copied so repeats stay independent, matching the map-style path where the dataset re-materializes a
864	        # fresh object per access.
865	        keys = list(batch)
866	        if len(batch[keys[0]]) < batch_size:
867	            return {key: [] for key in keys}
868	        repeated = {key: [] for key in keys}
869	        for _ in range(repeat_count):
870	            for values in zip(*(batch[key] for key in keys), strict=True):
871	                for _ in range(mini_repeat_count):
872	                    for key, value in zip(keys, values, strict=True):
873	                        repeated[key].append(copy.deepcopy(value))
874	        return repeated
875	
876	    return dataset.map(repeat_batch, batched=True, batch_size=batch_size)

880	def nanstd(tensor: torch.Tensor, dim: int | tuple[int, ...] | None = None, keepdim: bool = False) -> torch.Tensor:
881	    """
882	    Compute the standard deviation of a tensor, ignoring NaNs.
883	
884	    Args:
885	        tensor (`torch.Tensor`):
886	            Input tensor.
887	        dim (`int` or `tuple[int, ...]`, *optional*):
888	            Dimension(s) to reduce. Defaults to all dimensions.
889	        keepdim (`bool`, *optional*, defaults to `False`):
890	            Whether to keep reduced dimensions.
891	
892	    Returns:
893	        `torch.Tensor`:
894	            Standard deviation of the tensor, ignoring NaNs.
895	    """
896	    # Compute variance ignoring NaNs
897	    mean = torch.nanmean(tensor, dim=dim, keepdim=True)
898	    variance = torch.nanmean((tensor - mean) ** 2, dim=dim, keepdim=True)
899	    count = torch.sum(~torch.isnan(tensor), dim=dim, keepdim=True)  # count of non-NaN values
900	    correction = count / (count - 1)
901	    correction = torch.where(count > 1, correction, torch.full_like(correction, float("nan")))
902	    variance *= correction  # Bessel's correction
903	    std = torch.sqrt(variance)
904	    if keepdim:
905	        return std
906	    if dim is None:
907	        return std.squeeze()
908	    if isinstance(dim, int):
909	        return std.squeeze(dim)
910	    dims = [(d if d >= 0 else d + std.ndim) for d in dim]
911	    for d in sorted(dims, reverse=True):
912	        std = std.squeeze(d)
913	    return std

917	    tensor_dict: dict[str, torch.Tensor | None], num_chunks: int
918	) -> list[dict[str, torch.Tensor | None]]:

920	    Splits a dictionary of tensors along the first dimension into `num_chunks` equal parts.
921	
922	    Example:
923	    ```python
924	    >>> x = torch.arange(12).reshape(6, 2)
925	    >>> y = torch.arange(6).reshape(6, 1)

927	    >>> split_tensor_dict(tensor_dict, 3)

930	        {"x": tensor([[4, 5], [6, 7]]), "y": tensor([[2], [3]])},
931	        {"x": tensor([[ 8,  9], [10, 11]]), "y": tensor([[4], [5]])}
932	    ]
933	    ```
934	    """
935	    first_tensor = next(tensor for tensor in tensor_dict.values() if tensor is not None)
936	    chunk_size = first_tensor.shape[0] // num_chunks
937	    chunks = []
938	    for i in range(num_chunks):
939	        chunk_dict = {}
940	        for key, tensor in tensor_dict.items():
941	            if tensor is not None and (isinstance(tensor, list) or tensor.ndim > 0):
942	                chunk_dict[key] = tensor[i * chunk_size : (i + 1) * chunk_size]
943	            elif tensor is not None and tensor.ndim == 0:
944	                chunk_dict[key] = tensor
945	            else:
946	                chunk_dict[key] = None
947	        chunks.append(chunk_dict)

953	    Shuffles all sequence-like values in a dictionary along the first dimension in unison.
954	
955	    Example:
956	    ```python
957	    >>> x = torch.arange(6).reshape(3, 2)

2399	    def get_total_train_batch_size(self, args: TrainingArguments) -> int:
2400	        """Calculates total batch size (micro_batch * grad_accum * dp_world_size).
2401	
2402	        Accounts for all parallelism dimensions: TP, CP, and SP.
2403	
2404	        Formula: dp_world_size = world_size // (tp_size * cp_size * sp_size)
2405	
2406	        Where:
2407	        - TP (Tensor Parallelism): Model layers split across GPUs
2408	        - CP (Context Parallelism): Sequences split using Ring Attention (FSDP2)
2409	        - SP (Sequence Parallelism): Sequences split using ALST/Ulysses (DeepSpeed)
2410	
2411	        All dimensions are separate and multiplicative: world_size = dp_size * tp_size * cp_size * sp_size
2412	        """
2413	
2414	        dp_world_size = args.world_size // self.get_tp_size() // self.get_cp_size() // self.get_sp_size()
2415	        return self._train_batch_size * args.gradient_accumulation_steps * dp_world_size

718	class RepeatSampler(Sampler):
719	    """
720	    Sampler that repeats the indices of a dataset in a structured manner.
721	
722	    Args:
723	        data_source (`Sized`):
724	            Dataset to sample from.
725	        mini_repeat_count (`int`):
726	            Number of times to repeat each index per batch.
727	        batch_size (`int`, *optional*, defaults to `1`):
728	            Number of unique indices per batch.
729	        repeat_count (`int`, *optional*, defaults to `1`):
730	            Number of times to repeat the full sampling process.
731	        shuffle (`bool`, *optional*, defaults to `True`):
732	            Whether to shuffle the dataset.
733	        seed (`int`, *optional*):
734	            Random seed for reproducibility (only affects this sampler).
735	
736	    Example:
737	    ```python
738	    >>> sampler = RepeatSampler(["a", "b", "c", "d", "e", "f", "g"], mini_repeat_count=2, batch_size=3, repeat_count=4)
739	    >>> list(sampler)
740	    [4, 4, 3, 3, 0, 0,
741	     4, 4, 3, 3, 0, 0,
742	     4, 4, 3, 3, 0, 0,
743	     4, 4, 3, 3, 0, 0,
744	     1, 1, 2, 2, 6, 6,
745	     1, 1, 2, 2, 6, 6,
746	     1, 1, 2, 2, 6, 6,
747	     1, 1, 2, 2, 6, 6]
748	    ```
749	
750	    ```txt
751	    mini_repeat_count = 3
752	          -   -   -
753	         [0,  0,  0,  1,  1,  1,  2,  2,  2,  3,  3,  3,      |
754	          4,  4,  4,  5,  5,  5,  6,  6,  6,  7,  7,  7,      |
755	          8,  8,  8,  9,  9,  9, 10, 10, 10, 11, 11, 11,      |
756	                                                                repeat_count = 2
757	          0,  0,  0,  1,  1,  1,  2,  2,  2,  3,  3,  3,      |
758	          4,  4,  4,  5,  5,  5,  6,  6,  6,  7,  7,  7,      |
759	          8,  8,  8,  9,  9,  9, 10, 10, 10, 11, 11, 11, ...] |
760	          ---------   ---------   ---------   ---------
761	           ---------   ---------   ---------   ---------
762	            ---------   ---------   ---------   ---------
763	                         batch_size = 12
764	    ```
765	    """
766	
767	    def __init__(
768	        self,
769	        data_source: Sized,
770	        mini_repeat_count: int,
771	        batch_size: int = 1,
772	        repeat_count: int = 1,
773	        shuffle: bool = True,
774	        seed: int | None = None,
775	    ):
776	        self.data_source = data_source
777	        self.mini_repeat_count = mini_repeat_count
778	        self.batch_size = batch_size
779	        self.repeat_count = repeat_count
780	        self.num_samples = len(data_source)
781	        self.shuffle = shuffle
782	        self.seed = seed
783	
784	        if shuffle:
785	            self.generator = torch.Generator()  # Create a local random generator
786	            if seed is not None:
787	                self.generator.manual_seed(seed)
788	
789	    def __iter__(self):
790	        if self.shuffle:
791	            # E.g., [2, 4, 3, 1, 0, 6, 5] (num_samples = 7)
792	            indexes = torch.randperm(self.num_samples, generator=self.generator).tolist()
793	        else:
794	            indexes = list(range(self.num_samples))
795	
796	        #    [2, 4, 3, 1, 0, 6, 5]
797	        # -> [[2, 4, 3], [1, 0, 6], [5]]  (batch_size = 3)
798	        indexes = [indexes[i : i + self.batch_size] for i in range(0, len(indexes), self.batch_size)]
799	
800	        #    [[2, 4, 3], [1, 0, 6], [5]]
801	        # -> [[2, 4, 3], [1, 0, 6]]
802	        indexes = [chunk for chunk in indexes if len(chunk) == self.batch_size]
803	
804	        for chunk in indexes:
805	            for _ in range(self.repeat_count):
806	                for index in chunk:
807	                    for _ in range(self.mini_repeat_count):
808	                        yield index
809	
810	    def __len__(self) -> int:
811	        return (self.num_samples // self.batch_size) * self.batch_size * self.mini_repeat_count * self.repeat_count
812	
813	
814	def repeat_iterable_dataset(
815	    dataset: IterableDataset, mini_repeat_count: int, batch_size: int = 1, repeat_count: int = 1
816	):
817	    """
818	    Streaming counterpart of [`RepeatSampler`] for [`~datasets.IterableDataset`].
819	
820	    An [`~datasets.IterableDataset`] cannot be indexed, so a sampler cannot be attached to it. Instead of reordering
821	    indices, this reorders the *stream* itself with [`~datasets.IterableDataset.map`], producing records in exactly the
822	    same order that [`RepeatSampler`] yields indices for a map-style dataset with the same arguments. Because the
823	    transform stays chained to `dataset`, `set_epoch` propagates to an upstream [`~datasets.IterableDataset.shuffle`]
824	    and the order is reshuffled every epoch, as [`RepeatSampler`] does.
825	
826	    Shuffling is intentionally left out: it is handled upstream via [`~datasets.IterableDataset.shuffle`] (buffered
827	    shuffling), the streaming equivalent of the full permutation done by [`RepeatSampler`].
828	
829	    Args:
830	        dataset (`datasets.IterableDataset`):
831	            Dataset to stream from.
832	        mini_repeat_count (`int`):
833	            Number of times to repeat each record per batch.
834	        batch_size (`int`, *optional*, defaults to `1`):
835	            Number of unique records per batch.
836	        repeat_count (`int`, *optional*, defaults to `1`):
837	            Number of times to repeat the full batch.
838	
839	    Returns:
840	        `datasets.IterableDataset`: Dataset yielding the records of `dataset`, repeated and reordered.
841	
842	    Example:
843	    ```python
844	    >>> from datasets import IterableDataset
845	
846	    >>> dataset = IterableDataset.from_generator(lambda: ({"x": i} for i in range(7)))
847	    >>> repeated = repeat_iterable_dataset(dataset, mini_repeat_count=2, batch_size=3, repeat_count=4)
848	    >>> [record["x"] for record in repeated]
849	    [0, 0, 1, 1, 2, 2,
850	     0, 0, 1, 1, 2, 2,
851	     0, 0, 1, 1, 2, 2,
852	     0, 0, 1, 1, 2, 2,
853	     3, 3, 4, 4, 5, 5,
854	     3, 3, 4, 4, 5, 5,
855	     3, 3, 4, 4, 5, 5,
856	     3, 3, 4, 4, 5, 5]
857	    ```
858	    """
859	
860	    def repeat_batch(batch: dict) -> dict:
861	        # `batch` maps each column to a list of `batch_size` values (fewer for the trailing batch, which is dropped to
862	        # match RepeatSampler). Transpose it back to records, repeating them as RepeatSampler repeats indices. Records
863	        # are deep-copied so repeats stay independent, matching the map-style path where the dataset re-materializes a
864	        # fresh object per access.
865	        keys = list(batch)
866	        if len(batch[keys[0]]) < batch_size:
867	            return {key: [] for key in keys}
868	        repeated = {key: [] for key in keys}
869	        for _ in range(repeat_count):
870	            for values in zip(*(batch[key] for key in keys), strict=True):
871	                for _ in range(mini_repeat_count):
872	                    for key, value in zip(keys, values, strict=True):
873	                        repeated[key].append(copy.deepcopy(value))
874	        return repeated
875	
876	    return dataset.map(repeat_batch, batched=True, batch_size=batch_size)
877

879	# torch.nanstd doesn't exist, so we define it here
880	def nanstd(tensor: torch.Tensor, dim: int | tuple[int, ...] | None = None, keepdim: bool = False) -> torch.Tensor:
881	    """
882	    Compute the standard deviation of a tensor, ignoring NaNs.
883	
884	    Args:
885	        tensor (`torch.Tensor`):
886	            Input tensor.
887	        dim (`int` or `tuple[int, ...]`, *optional*):
888	            Dimension(s) to reduce. Defaults to all dimensions.
889	        keepdim (`bool`, *optional*, defaults to `False`):
890	            Whether to keep reduced dimensions.
891	
892	    Returns:
893	        `torch.Tensor`:
894	            Standard deviation of the tensor, ignoring NaNs.
895	    """
896	    # Compute variance ignoring NaNs
897	    mean = torch.nanmean(tensor, dim=dim, keepdim=True)
898	    variance = torch.nanmean((tensor - mean) ** 2, dim=dim, keepdim=True)
899	    count = torch.sum(~torch.isnan(tensor), dim=dim, keepdim=True)  # count of non-NaN values
900	    correction = count / (count - 1)
901	    correction = torch.where(count > 1, correction, torch.full_like(correction, float("nan")))
902	    variance *= correction  # Bessel's correction

3039	    def get_off_policy_mask(
3040	        advantages: torch.Tensor,
3041	        per_token_logps: torch.Tensor,
3042	        sampling_per_token_logps: torch.Tensor,
3043	        mask: torch.Tensor,
3044	        off_policy_threshold: float,
3045	    ) -> torch.Tensor:
3046	        """
3047	        Computes the Off-Policy Sequence Mask from DeepSeek-V3.2 paper. Returns a (B, 1) tensor where 1.0 indicates
3048	        "Keep" and 0.0 indicates "Drop".
3049	        """
3050	        # forward KL div: log(pi_old) - log(pi_theta)
3051	        kl_div = sampling_per_token_logps - per_token_logps.detach()
3052	        # Tokens vLLM could not score carry NaN and provide no KL evidence. Left in, the sequence mean is NaN,
3053	        # `avg_seq_kl <= off_policy_threshold` is then False, and a negative-advantage sequence would be dropped
3054	        # on the strength of a single unscorable token.
3055	        kl_div = torch.nan_to_num(kl_div, nan=0.0)
3056	        # Sequence-level Mean KL (ignoring prompt+padding)
3057	        seq_kl_sum = (kl_div * mask).sum(dim=1, keepdim=True)
3058	        avg_seq_kl = seq_kl_sum / mask.sum(dim=1, keepdim=True).clamp(min=1.0)
3059	        # Keep if (Advantage >= 0) OR (KL <= delta)
3060	        is_pos_adv = advantages >= 0
3061	        is_low_kl = avg_seq_kl <= off_policy_threshold
3062	        return (is_pos_adv | is_low_kl).to(dtype=mask.dtype)  # (B, 1)

3066	    def get_gamma_weights(
3067	        advantages: torch.Tensor,
3068	        log_ratio_per_token: torch.Tensor,
3069	        mask: torch.Tensor,
3070	        importance_sampling_ratio: torch.Tensor | None,  # (B, T)
3071	        k_pos: float = 2.0,
3072	        lambda_pos: float = 3.0,
3073	        k_neg: float = 3.0,
3074	        lambda_neg: float = 2.0,
3075	    ) -> torch.Tensor:
3076	        """
3077	        Computes the Gamma weights for the VESPO loss. For reference:
3078	            φ(w) = e^λ × w^k × e^{-λw} is the gamma weighting (normalized so φ(1)=1)
3079	                with w = sequence-level importance sampling ratio
3080	        note: we will compute φ(w) in log space
3081	
3082	        φ(w) is detached via @torch.no_grad(), only acts as gradient scaling coefficient
3083	
3084	        VESPO loss = -φ(w) × A × log_prob, gradient naturally gives φ(w) × A × ∇log π
3085	        """
3086	        # reducing clamp range directly to log(1e-8) ~ -18.42, to avoid recomputing log_w=log(w.clamp(min=1e-8)) later
3087	        # This is solely for matching truthfully the original implementation, otherwise keeping -20 could be fine.
3088	        lower_clamp = math.log(1e-8)
3089	
3090	        # Sequence-level log ratio Σ log(π_θ/π_old) (not a mean like for `log_importance_weights`)
3091	        log_ratio_clamped = torch.clamp(log_ratio_per_token, -20.0, 20.0)
3092	        seq_log_ratio = torch.sum(log_ratio_clamped * mask, dim=-1, keepdim=True)  # (B, 1)
3093	
3094	        # Apply token-level TIS or MIS correction (in log space)
3095	        if importance_sampling_ratio is not None:
3096	            log_is_ratio = torch.clamp(torch.log(importance_sampling_ratio), lower_clamp, 20.0)
3097	            # log(w) = log(π_θ/π_old) + log(π_old/π_sampler)
3098	            seq_log_ratio += torch.sum(log_is_ratio, dim=-1, keepdim=True)
3099	
3100	        log_w_seq = torch.clamp(seq_log_ratio, lower_clamp, 20.0)
3101	        w_seq = torch.exp(log_w_seq)
3102	
3103	        # compute k and lambda based on advantage sign
3104	        is_nonneg_adv = advantages >= 0
3105	        k_seq = torch.where(is_nonneg_adv, k_pos, k_neg)
3106	        lambda_seq = torch.where(is_nonneg_adv, lambda_pos, lambda_neg).clamp(min=1e-4)
3107	
3108	        # log(φ(w)) = λ + k × log(w) - λ × w
3109	        log_phi = lambda_seq + k_seq * log_w_seq - lambda_seq * w_seq
3110	        phi_seq = torch.exp(log_phi).nan_to_num(nan=0.0, posinf=0.0, neginf=0.0)
3111	
3112	        return phi_seq  # (B, 1)
